News.title: Cops dig up church car park after tip-off in cold case of missing mum-of-two who vanished 34 years ago
News.content:
FRESH SEARCH Cops dig up church car park after tip-off in cold case of missing mum-of-two who vanished 34 years ago

COPS investigating the disappearance of a mum-of-two who went missing 34 years ago have dug up a car park in search of clues.

Patricia Hall, then aged 39, vanished on January 25, 1992, during a family day out in Ripon, North Yorkshire.



West Yorkshire Police have started digging near Moravian Church in Fulneck, Leeds, after the team received reports of new “information” about Patricia’s disappearance.

However, “nothing of note” has yet been found, cops said today.



Police have released images of the site, with workers pictured standing next to several large black bags.

Although detectives have not yet recovered a body, an inquest into her death was launched in April this year at Wakefield Coroner’s Court.





Coroner Oliver Longstaff explained how Patricia’s sister, Christine Weatherhead, had requested a new application to hold an inquest.

Patricia’s husband Keith was previously tried for murder – after reports of their tumultuous marriage emerged – but was found not guilty in 1994.

In a disturbing interview with an undercover cop, Keith claimed to have killed his wife – but the jury was never allowed to hear the recorded “admission”.

He later backtracked and said that he had only confessed to killing her to please his new girlfriend – the undercover cop – in a bid to convince her Patricia wasn’t coming back and they could continue their relationship.

In a police interview, Keith said: “When I left that car, I was going to go back and say, ‘You know what I said is a load of ooish, don’t you? Made up entirely to please you?’ And I should have done, really.”



The inquest heard how there had been no sightings of her since her disappearance and no “circumstantial evidence” to suggest she was still alive – such as use of a bank account or contact with family.

Cops stated that the car park dig is purely speculative, as the team attempts to recover information.

A spokesperson said: “Officers from West Yorkshire Police’s Major Investigation Review Team are currently examining a site at Fulneck, Pudsey, in connection with the disappearance of Patricia Hall in Leeds in 1992.

“The search for potential evidence follows recent information received by the team and is being carried out on a speculative basis.

“There is nothing to suggest any link to the Moravian Church, which owns the site.”



Assistant Chief Constable Sarah Jones said Patricia Hall’s family had been informed about the latest developments.

She said: “We are conscious of the understandable public focus that this activity is likely to attract in this high-profile case.

“Patricia’s family have been informed, and we will be keeping them updated.

“We obviously have a duty to act on any new information we receive but at this stage we are keeping an open mind.”

“The Major Investigation Review Team carried out a thorough cold case review into Patricia’s disappearance which concluded last year without establishing any new lines of enquiry.”

She added that the team would welcome any new or additional information that could assist the inquiry.

News.title: Chaos on major motorway as lorry fire shuts lanes and drivers stuck in hour-long delays
News.content:
A LORRY has caught fire on a major motorway causing traffic to grind to a halt.

The M25 has been closed off in the anticlockwise direction between J6 and J5 in Kent.

Hour-long delays are expected and tailbacks are said to have reached J8.

Local lanes are also reportedly experiencing congestion as motorists reroute.





A fire brigade has been called to the scene and is currently tackling the blaze, with smoke seen rising across the M25.

Images show three fire engines parked across the lanes by J5, with thick traffic pictured behind.

The fire is understood to be located in the cargo hold of the lorry.

It follows another closure on the M23 in Surrey in the northbound direction between J9 and J9a this afternoon.



Emergency services were called to tackle a van fire.

Delays of more than 10 minutes and one mile of congestion were reported.

News.title: Australian PM accused of ‘crude joke’ about Japan’s female leader’s ‘melons’ as diplomatic row erupts
News.content:
THE Australian PM has been accused of making a crude joke about the Japanese leader’s “melons” – sparking a furious diplomatic row.

Anthony Albanese was appearing on the Bush Deep podcast when he was asked about the worst gift he had received while overseas.



After briefly pausing, he said he had recently received a gift that was “pretty strange but ended up being quite good”.

The gift was two royal melons given to him by Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi during an official visit in May.



During the podcast, host Nikki Osbourne asked Mr Albanese how Ms Takaichi had managed to “smuggle” the melons through Australian customs.

The Australian comedian then made a suggestive gesture with both hands in front of her chest.



Mr Albanese quickly mimicked the gesture before joking that Ms Takaichi had brought “a couple of melons… as you do”.

Later in the podcast, Osbourne made the startling observation that the Japanese leader had “come in looking like Pamela Anderson“.



Mr Albanese did not object to the comment.

The clip has since sparked outrage in Japan, with former Australian ambassador to Japan Shingo Yamagami penning a scathing opinion piece.

Yamagami, who served as Japan’s ambassador to Australia from 2020 to 2023, said Mr Albanese’s comments were “not only ungracious” but betrayed “the close bonds of our two nations”.

He described the comments and gestures as “appalling” and criticised the Prime Minister for failing to show proper respect for the gift.

“A crown melon is the most prized fruit in Japan and treasured as something special,” he said.



Mr Albanese has also faced criticism from opposition politicians, who branded his comments “grubby” and “beneath the office of prime minister”.

Opposition leader Angus Taylor said: “They were insulting and the prime minister should make a personal apology.”

But senior cabinet ministers have rushed to his defence.

Social Services Minister Tanya Plibersek said: “Japan is a very important strategic and economic partner … and I think the former ambassador is wrong in his interpretation.”

Health Minister Mark Butler also stressed Australia’s close economic and security ties with Japan.



He said: “It’s very close. It involves constant communication between our two countries, two at the highest level.

“I know Prime Minister Albanese feels the deepest respect for that relationship.”

It is not the first time Mr Albanese has found himself at the centre of controversy over comments made on a podcast.

During the same episode, Osbourne asked him whom he would “shag, marry and date” between Australian icons Kylie Minogue, Nicole Kidman and Rhonda Burchmore.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

After initially hesitating, the Prime Minister gave the crude response: Minogue “for all of the above”.



He later issued a one-line apology, saying he was “unequivocally” sorry for the incident.

News.title: Child’s body found at house as man, 31, and woman, 32, charged with preventing lawful burial
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

TRAGIC FIND Child’s body found at house as man, 31, and woman, 32, charged with preventing lawful burial

A 31-YEAR-OLD man and a woman, aged 32, have been charged with preventing a lawful burial after a child’s body was found at a house.

Cops discovered the body at a property in Southend, Essex, on August 7, following a welfare concern raised by social services.

Sophie Dean, 31, of Coates House, Kenway, Southend, and James Thorpe, 32, of Frobisher Way, Shoeburyness, have been charged with preventing a lawful and decent burial of a dead body.

The charge relates to a time period between July 3, 2025 and August 6, 2026.





Mr Thorpe has also been charged with obstruction of a constable in the execution of their duty, said Essex Police.

Both appeared at Southend Magistrates’ Court on August 10 and were remanded in custody.

The pair are due to appear next at Basildon Crown Court on September 7, cops added.

An Essex Police spokesperson said: “The investigation into the child’s death will continue to be led by detectives from our Crime and Public Protection Command.



“We would also encourage anyone with information that could assist us and who has not yet spoken to us to please come forward and do so, quoting investigation number 42/125225/26.”

No further details about the child or the circumstances of their death have been released.

News.title: Meet Russia’s sexiest war influencer – the soldier’s wife and glamorous Kremlin puppet whose first word was ‘Putin’
News.content:
RUSSIA’S sexiest war influencer is a soldier’s wife and glamorous Kremlin puppet, whose first word was “Putin”.

One of the Russian President’s most effective propagandists is 25-year-old Maria Chadina.



While appearing in designer clothes and immaculate make-up, along with a velvety voice she promotes Russia’s campaign in the war with Ukraine to hundreds of thousands of her followers on social media.

But behind the polished photographs and romantic videos there is an online lifestyle warrior guided by a Kremlin-linked indoctrination agency bent on turning Putin’s illegal invasion into something glamorous, fashionable – and even sexy.



Unlike Putin’s army of ranting male television firebrands who threaten Britain with nuclear destruction and Ukraine with ceasing to exist, Chadina speaks softly about love, marriage and patriotism from stylish apartments and fashionable cafés.

Yet her message is the same, stressing there is no alternative to Putin’s war which has already killed and maimed 1.5million of his own people.

She tells followers that Ukraine’s not a real country, denies Russia is politically repressive, and reassures followers that Putin will not order another mobilisation even as plans seem afoot for exactly this ominous mass call-up.

She has also demanded revenge after Ukrainian attacks, once tearfully declaring: “It doesn’t matter how. Even launch Oreshnik” – a reference to Russia’s feared nuclear-capable ballistic missile.



Chadina hits back at suggestions that she is the Kremlin’s glamorous new weapon.

In a sarcastic video addressing the allegations, she opened in English: “Thank you for your attention to my humble person, but you’re mistaken.

“I’m not Putin’s glamorous propaganda.



“I’m just a simple Russian girl. And my name is Masha [Maria] Chadina. Thanks. Grand merci.”

Switching to Russian, she joked that she was born in 2000, the year Putin came to power and added: “My first word, by the way, wasn’t ‘Mum’, but ‘Putin’.”

She thanked her history tutor for ensuring she understood why the war started.

She means the Kremlin-approved version that blames Ukraine and the West.

Chadina then joked that her soldier husband Vova [Vladimir] had gone to war “just so I could start a blog”.



She hoped “the Kremlin will finally recognise me.

“And, as they say, finally, 12 points goes to Russia.”

Chadina’s rise from provincial reporter to an influencer with almost 400,000 followers on Instagram – officially banned in Russian – is choreographed by Base Media, a shadowy pro-Putin agency which boasts: “We create media that influences society.”

The company is owned by the mother of Sargis Mirzakhanyan, a pro-government political strategist previously accused of promoting Kremlin interests among European politicians.

Base Media also produces content involving notorious Russian pranksters Vovan and Lexus, who have repeatedly duped Western politicians and celebrities while pushing Moscow-friendly narratives.



An employee of Dialog, an organisation helping the Kremlin manage online messaging, told Novaya Gazeta Europe that Chadina initially attracted followers organically before pro-Putin professionals stepped in to refine her image.

“She was in the right place at the right time,” said a source. “Her channel and videos were just right: a sweet, beautiful young wife of a [war] soldier, a patriot.”

She is also linked to a project by Defenders of the Fatherland, headed by Putin’s niece Anna Tsivileva, who is also Deputy Defence Minister.

With a daughter from her first marriage, she met her second husband, Russian Railways employee Vladimir Chadin, on a dating app.

He soon signed up to fight in Ukraine and has reportedly been wounded twice.



Videos showing Chadina waiting anxiously for Vladimir and embracing him during reunions have attracted hundreds of thousands of views, particularly from other soldiers’ wives.

She turns on its head the stereotype of the impoverished and forgotten Russian military spouse.

Alongside a glamorous photograph, she wrote: “Let’s stop thinking that the wives of SVO [war] soldiers are necessarily marginalised, uneducated, without opinions and without the right to feel like women.

“We can be beautiful and sexy. While remaining faithful and loving. Devoted to our husbands. Agreed?”

Her posts mix cosmetics, clothes and domestic romance with fundraisers for Russian troops and carefully packaged pro-war messages.



She has appeared at Putin’s annual televised press conference and was reportedly granted access to a prisoner exchange with Ukraine.

In May, in an elegant black dress she collected a national internet-content award for Russia’s fastest-growing political blog of 2025.

Dedicating it to Vladimir at the front, she said through tears: “Vova, we won. And we will all win. Victory will be ours.”

Pro-war image-makers in Moscow evidently see her mix of beauty, vulnerability and carefully controlled patriotism as a more potent propaganda tool than hoary old state broadcasters like doyen of the bile merchants Vladimir Solovyov.

Russian journalist and propaganda researcher Maria Borzunova said Maria appears to share the pain of ordinary military families.



“She’s supposedly one of us because she’s also waiting for her lover to return from the war,” she said.

“She’s not Vladimir Solovyov telling [everyone] how to live from a cosy studio.”

One critical commenter said: “This is “Solovyov in a skirt.”

Another mocked her: “With tears in her eyes, she remembers her husband, who kills people in a foreign country.”

Fashion journalist Katya Fedorova said Chadina had transformed the soldier’s wife into a secular, European-looking figure with “a beautiful apartment, fashionable clothes and a fancy café”.



She added: “She shows that a military wife can be a very modern woman, making this image more elite.

“That, in my opinion, is a major victory for Russian propaganda.”

Chadina has been accused of “the most dangerous form of propaganda – people get so caught up in the beautiful imagery they fail to analyse what Maria is saying.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Chadina gleefully reposted the criticism by the liberal Novaya Gazeta Europe.

“They are afraid of me!” she posted with a smiling emoji.

News.title: What do UK heat warnings mean? Map shows where health alerts are in place as Met Office considers red warning
News.content:
AMBER heat health alerts have been announced across the majority of England.

And with another heatwave forecast this week, the Met Office is considering issuing a rare red extreme heat warning – here’s everything you need to know about what the different alerts mean.



Where are heat health warnings in place in the UK?

The prolonged high temperatures and lack of rain have left more than half of England and all of Wales facing official drought conditions.

And the Met Office says that temperatures could reach 36C in parts of East Anglia and south-east England by Thursday.



On Monday, the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) issued updated heat health alerts – which are provided in partnership with the Met Office – across much of England.

As you can see on our interactive map below, UKHSA amber heat health alerts have been issued for eight regions, while a yellow alert is in place for one.



UKHSA acting public health consultant, Polly Ashmore, said: “Periods of hot weather can result in serious health outcomes, especially for older adults, and it is therefore important that everyone takes sensible precautions while enjoying the sun.

“We are urging health and social care services in affected regions to ensure they are prepared, and reminding people to look out for elderly relatives, neighbours, and those with underlying health conditions, making sure they are aware of the forecast and following the necessary advice.

“Simple steps such as staying hydrated, avoiding the sun during the hottest part of the day, and keeping your home cool are some of the key ways to help keep yourself and others safe during periods of hot weather.”

Separately, the Met Office is responsible for the National Severe Weather Warning Service (NSWWS), which issues yellow, amber and red warnings for circumstances like thunderstorms and rain.



It can also declare amber and red warnings for for extreme heat, as the forecaster did earlier this year.

Met Office meteorologist Tom Morgan said: “We sometimes issue extreme heat warnings, amber and red warnings, which we did back in June, so that’s under consideration at the moment.”

While the UKHSA alerts focus on the heat’s impact on public health, the Met Office’s NSWWS warnings cover the wider impacts of the heat to protect lives and property.

What do the UK heat health colours mean?

According to the Met Office website, the health alerts that the UKHSA issues in partnership with the forecaster carry the following meanings:

Green (summer preparedness)

No alert will be issued as the conditions are likely to have minimal impact on health.



However, during periods where the risk is minimal it is important that organisations ensure that they have plans in place and are prepared to respond should an alert (yellow, amber, or red) be issued.

Yellow (response)

These alerts cover a range of situations.

Yellow alerts may be issued during periods of heat which would be unlikely to impact most people, but those you are particularly vulnerable (e.g. the elderly with multiple health conditions and on multiple medications) and are likely to struggle to cope and where action is required within the health and social care sector specifically.

A yellow alert may also be issued if the confidence in the weather forecast is low, but there could be more significant impacts if the worst-case scenario is realised.

In this situation the alert may be upgraded as the confidence in both the weather forecast and the likelihood of observing those impacts improves.



Amber (enhanced response)

An amber alert would represent a situation in which the expected impacts are likely to be felt across the whole health service, with potential for the whole population to be at risk and where other sectors apart from health may also start to observe impacts, indicating that a coordinated response is required.

In addition, in some circumstances a National Severe Weather Warning Service (NSWWS) Extreme Heat warning may be issued in conjunction with and aligned to the HHA.

This situation would indicate that significant impacts are expected across multiple sectors.

Red (emergency response)

A red alert would indicate significant risk to life for even the healthy population.

A red warning would be issued in conjunction with and aligned to a red NSWWS Extreme Heat warning.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Severe impacts would be expected across all sectors with a coordinated response essential.

News.title: Over 70% of England declares drought ahead of 36C temperatures this week – check full list of 4 new regions affected
News.content:
NEARLY three quarters of England has declared drought ahead of 36C temperatures this week.

The National Drought Group has moved seven more areas to drought status, taking the total to 45 million Brits in affected areas.

The whole of the East Midlands, Lincolnshire & Northamptonshire, Kent & East Sussex, and Solent & the South Downs has now declared drought status.



These regions join seven other parts of England, alongside the entirety of Wales, to experience the consistently dry conditions.



Most of the country is experiencing a flash drought, which has been provoked by the ongoing dry conditions and higher temperatures.

Around 45 million people in England are in an area that’s declared drought, with over 27 million living under hosepipe ban restrictions, which have been enforced by nine water companies.

The North East and Yorkshire have also been moved into the prolonged dry weather category, the stage before drought.

Changes by the National Drought Group to alter the drought status come after England recorded the driest July since records began in 1836.

Rainfall in July has ranged from one per cent of the expected amount in south-east England, to 26 per cent in north-west England.

Parts of Hampshire, the Isle of Wight and West Sussex have not had a rain day for 59 days.

Brits are also bracing for the fifth heatwave of the year, as temperatures are set to soar as high as 36C on Thursday.

Amber heat health alerts have been issued for most of England, with the Met Office currently considering whether to issue a rare red extreme heat warning due to the high temperatures.

In response to the change, Water Minister Emma Hardy said: “We know how challenging this summer has been, especially for our hard-working farmers who are at the sharp end of climate change and an increasing number of floods and droughts.

“We are stepping up our support including working to make it easier for farmers to build more on-site irrigation reservoirs.

“We are also delivering long-term change in the water industry to reduce leaks and deliver nine new reservoirs and water transfer schemes to secure supplies.



“As we move through this period of drought, I expect water companies to take every available step to minimise leakage and support customers in using water wisely.

“I also want to thank people for following the restrictions, where in place, as they are an important tool to safeguard essential water supplies and protect the environment.”

News.title: Student cop, 23, arrested for ‘kidnapping and raping woman in her 20s’ following police chase on motorway
News.content:
COP ARREST Student cop, 23, arrested for ‘kidnapping and raping woman in her 20s’ following police chase on motorway

A 23-YEAR-OLD student police officer has been arrested on suspicion of rape and kidnap after a frantic police chase on a major motorway.

The cop, serving with Greater Manchester Police, was detained in West Yorkshire on Saturday while off duty after the pursuit on the M62.

A 999 call had been received shortly before 10.20pm in which a woman in her 20s could be heard “in distress” in a vehicle in the Manchester area, said the force.

Officers traced the suspect’s personal vehicle and began a pursuit.





The 23-year-old student cop was then arrested on suspicion of rape, kidnap and dangerous driving, added police.

The officer, who has been suspended, remains in custody for questioning.

Most read in The Sun code red What UK heat health alerts mean as Met Office considers red warning

Specialist officers and various agencies are supporting the woman, who is in her 20s.

The force has made a voluntary referral to the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC), GMP said.



Assistant Chief Constable Mark Dexter said: “This is quite clearly a deeply concerning and disturbing incident that we are fully investigating with specialist resources to ensure the victim receives support and justice.

“I can give our full commitment to working with the Crown Prosecution Service to bring this case to court as quickly as possible, as well as accelerating the necessary misconduct proceedings within the regulations.

“Thousands of the men and women in GMP work every day to protect the public. I know they, like me, will be shocked and angered by this news.

“Our Professional Standards Directorate has conducted an initial review and found his vetting was completed without any reason for concern.



“This does not, however, lessen the severity of these allegations.

“All necessary and decisive action will be taken in the interest of the victim and the public.”

The matter has also been referred by GMP to the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC).

News.title: Trainee cop arrested on rape and kidnap charges after 'dangerous' car chase
News.content:
Trainee cop arrested on rape and kidnap charges after 'dangerous' car chase

A 23-year-old trainee police officer was arrested on suspicion of kidnap, rape, and dangerous driving and remains in custody, following a high speed chase on the M62

View Image A man has been detained by Greater Manchester Police (Image: Kenny Brown | Manchester Evening News)

A trainee police officer has been arrested on suspicion of raping and kidnapping a woman following a high speed car chase.

Greater Manchester Police said the serving officer, 23, was detained following a pursuit involving his own vehicle on the M62 in West Yorkshire at the weekend.

Officers were responding to call at 10.18pm on Saturday where a woman "could be heard to be in distress in a vehicle", said the force.

The man was arrested on suspicion of kidnap, rape, and dangerous driving and remains in custody. And a woman in her 20s is receiving support from specialist officers.

A statement from GMP read: "Detectives are questioning a serving GMP student officer who was arrested in West Yorkshire on suspicion of rape over the weekend.

"The 23-year-old man, who was a student officer still in training, was stopped in his personal vehicle while off-duty following a pursuit on the M62.

"The pursuit followed a 999 call at 10.18pm on Saturday 8 August where a woman could be heard to be in distress in a vehicle in the Manchester area.

"Responding officers were quick to trace the suspected vehicle and a pursuit began. When the vehicle was stopped, the man was arrested on suspicion of kidnap, rape and dangerous driving.

"He remains in a Greater Manchester custody suite for questioning. The victim – a woman in her 20s – was safeguarded at the scene. Specialist officers and support agencies are working with her at this distressing time.

"He has been suspended and we have made a voluntary referral to the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC)."

Assistant Chief Constable Mark Dexter said: “This is quite clearly a deeply concerning and disturbing incident that we are fully investigating with specialist resources to ensure the victim receives support and justice.

“I can give our full commitment to working with the Crown Prosecution Service to bring this case to court as quickly as possible, as well as accelerating the necessary misconduct proceedings within the regulations.

News.title: New Forest fire - live: Wildlife haven could take 'decades' to recover as 120 firefighters tackle blaze
News.content:
A massive wildfire has scorched the New Forest after a lorry caught fire with the flames spreading to heathland as drivers ran for their lives with children in their arms

A devastating wildfire has scorched the New Forest with experts now warning that precious heathland - a haven for wild ponies, deer, and rare birds - could take decades to recover.

A spokesperson for the New Forest National Park Authority said it would mean a tragic loss of rare species and biodiversity. Drivers were forced to run for their lives with children in their arms as flames tore towards them on Sunday night with police telling them to abandon their cars if they "want to live".

One driver, Robert Green said: "People abandoned cars, running away on the opposite carriageway carrying kids. Our side was trying to turn around and move back through the middle of the cars but it was chaos."

The A31 remains closed in both directions due to the wildfire. Some 12 miles of the road is shut as it passes some of the most stunning parts of the national park and attractions like Paultons Park and Bolderwood Deer Sanctuary.

News.title: Murder victim's family will be 'living in fear' if killer is released and claim they'll never find the body
News.content:
Murder victim's family will be 'living in fear' if killer is released and claim they'll never find the body

The family of murdered Linda Razzell said they would be left living in fear if killer Glyn was released, and any hope of finding her body would be lost

View 3 Images Cat Razzell arrives at the High Court to plead for her mum's killer to be kept behind bars. Picture by Ian Vogler (Image: Ian Vogler / Daily Mirror)

The family of murdered Linda Razzell told the High Court all hope of finding her body will be lost if her killer is released from prison.

‌



Glyn Razzell, now 67, was jailed for a minimum of almost 16 years in 2003 for the murder of his estranged wife Linda. But for more than two decades he has refused to say what he did with her body. The mum-of-four disappeared on her way to work at Swindon College, Wiltshire, in March 2002, amid divorce proceedings. She was last seen parking her car.

‌



The Parole Board ruled three times from 2019 that Razzell should remain behind bars, but in April decided he could be released on licence. The Ministry of Justice then referred the decision to the High Court, telling a hearing on Monday that it should be reversed as the Parole Board failed to consider Razzell's risk properly.

‌



View 3 Images Linda Razzell, 41, vanished without trace on her way to work in Swindon, in May 2002 and was last seen parking her car. (Image: PA)

British couple jailed in Iran over espionage claims end hunger strike as worried son says it's a cry for help READ MORE :

Razzell attended the hearing in London and sat in the dock wearing a dark blue suit. He is opposing the bid to challenge his release. In a recording of her victim impact statement played to the court, Julie Westmore, Mrs Razzell's cousin, said that Razzell was a "master manipulator" who has "always failed to take responsibility for his actions".

She said: "The major impact on myself and our family would be the complete loss of trust in the justice system of this country if Glyn Razzell was released without revealing where Linda's remains are. It would quite simply be wrong."

‌



She continued: "We will not feel safe if Glyn Razzell is released. We know him to be a violent man and an accomplished liar."

View 3 Images Glyn Razzell's victim's family say they would not feel safe if he was released (Image: PA)

The Parole Board's decision came despite Helen's Law, which is named after Helen McCourt, who vanished on her way home from work in 1988. This law requires the Parole Board to take into consideration a killer's refusal to disclose where they hid their victim's body. Ms Westmore continued that Helen's Law meant "it has at last been recognised that it does matter when a murderer refuses to reveal where someone's remains are".

‌



She continued: "If Glyn Razzell remains in prison, it will be the incentive he needs to eventually do the right thing. It will be the right thing for everyone concerned, himself included. If Glyn Razzell is released now, all hope of ever finding Linda's remains will be lost."

Razzell, of Crewkerne, Somerset, has always denied being responsible for the killing, and a Parole Board panel found in 2023 that he "does not want to lose his desired status of being a 'wrongly convicted murderer'". In its April decision, a Parole Board panel said that it had "serious doubts" about Razzell's honesty and that there was a "very significant" risk in the context of relationships, but said this was "not imminent". It decided that he would comply with licence conditions as he was "strongly motivated not to return to custody".

The Ministry of Justice could refer a Parole Board's decision to release a prisoner to the High Court if it believes the release would undermine public confidence in the parole system, and the court must be satisfied that imprisonment is no longer necessary for the protection of the public.

‌



Tristan Jones KC, for the MoJ, said that Razzell had made a "degree of progress", and that professionals who worked with him supported his release, but that the Parole Board's report "loses sight of the fact that he has not been honest or transparent".

He continued: "Mr Razzell is a deeply deceitful individual who carried out a campaign of violence against Linda, some of it witnessed by their children, and then planned and carried out her murder. He is so attached to his narrative of innocence that he is willing to continue inflicting pain on the victims."

The barrister also said that proposed licence conditions "cannot fully address the risks" Razzell poses.

‌



Matthew Stanbury, for Razzell, told the court in written submissions that the Parole Board's decision was "detailed and thorough", and that the MoJ's case "comes close to treating denial as conclusive to risk".

He said: "The claimant's case is predicated on wrong assumptions or assertions that the defendant's denial of his offending, and attendant non-completion of offending behaviour programmes, are a bar to release.

"Both factors were properly considered and weighed by an experienced Parole Board panel which considered the countervailing factors and matters in the round. There is no, or no sufficiently cogent, basis for departing from the panel's decision."

Article continues below

The hearing before Mrs Justice Cheema-Grubb is due to conclude on Tuesday.

News.title: Drought declared in 11 key areas of England as 45 MILLION people urged to save water by any means necessary
News.content:
Most of England is now in drought affecting around 45 million people.

It was revealed on Monday that a massive 71.3 per cent of England is now in drought as we head for the fifth record-breaking heatwave of the year. The National Drought Group held a meeting today after the National Farmers Union warned that continuing dry weather could lead to some food shortages. Farmers reported their earliest harvests in 20 years, with reduced yields.

The group, made up of Government ministers, water companies, regulators and agricultural bodies, revealed almost three-quarters of England is now in drought and warned conditions were "worsening' and there would be "long-lasting impacts on our environment". They said all regions of the country are now experiencing pressure on their water resources because of the extreme dry weather-and high demand. The drought is now affecting agriculture, public supplies, navigation, and the environment.

View 20 Images Great Massingham near King's Lynn, Norfolk, residents launched an appeal to raise £15,000 to clear silt from their depleted pond called Scotsman's Pit (Image: Chris Bishop / SWNS)

‌



Wildfires break out across Britain with families told to run for their lives READ MORE :

Car washes and gym pools could be closed under drought-triggered water rationing READ MORE :

Rainfall totals for July, ranged from 1% of the expected average for south-east England to 26% in north-west England. Some parts of Hampshire, Isle of Wight and West Sussex have not had a rain day for 59 days. England has recorded its driest July in 190 years, since records began in 1836 with this year seeing 34 days where temperatures have reached 30C or above somewhere in England, including 13 consecutive days in July.

And there are warnings of more dry weather and another heatwave on the way, with temperatures soaring to 36C and above in some areas.

View 20 Images An aerial view of the blaze at the Holme Fen Nature Reserve today (Image: Getty Images)

The emergency drought group announced that East Midlands, Lincolnshire & Northamptonshire, Kent & East Sussex, and Solent & the South Downs were the latest regions to move into drought status. They follow in the footsteps of East Anglia, Hertfordshire and the whole of London, Thames Valley, Devon & Cornwall, Wessex (covering Dorset, Somerset, Wiltshire, and south Gloucestershire) and The West Midlands.

‌



View 20 Images More than two-thirds of England are now in an official drought (Image: PA Wire)

While areas in prolonged dry weather are: Cumbria & Lancashire, Greater Manchester, Merseyside & Cheshire, North East and Yorkshire. This takes the total to 45 million people in a drought area with more than 27 million people now living under restrictions on water use.

View 20 Images Holme Fen is known as the lowest point in the United Kingdom, at 9 feet below sea level (Image: Getty Images)

Tony Grayling, Strategic Drought Lead at the Environment Agency and Chair of the National Drought Group, said: “Drought conditions are worsening and will continue to do so until we see significant and sustained rainfall. We know the hot and dry weather is taking a real toll on farming and there will be long-lasting impacts on our environment. We want everyone to stay safe and hydrated over the summer, but we need everyone’s help in using a little less water to make sure our current water reserves last. Every drop we can save is a drop more for your local farmers, local wildlife and local rivers.”

‌



Full list of areas in England currently in a drought East Midlands Lincolnshire & Northamptonshire Kent & East Sussex Solent & the South Downs East Anglia Hertfordshire The whole of London Thames Valley Devon & Cornwall Wessex (covering Dorset, Somerset, Wiltshire, and south Gloucestershire) The West Midlands

Water Minister Emma Hardy has told water companies to do more to cut leaks, which increase in the hot weather as pipes move in dry soils. The public are being urged to take small steps to reduce water consumption – such as turning off taps when brushing teeth or fixing a leaking toilet.

View 20 Images Plymouth Hoe, Devon, looking very dry (Image: William Dax / SWNS)

Ms Hardy, who attended the National Drought Group, said: “We know how challenging this summer has been, especially for our hard-working farmers who are at the sharp end of climate change and an increasing number of floods and droughts.

‌



View 20 Images Sunseekers at Brockwell Lido in south London (Image: Jordan Pettitt/PA Wire)

“We are stepping up our support including working to make it easier for farmers to build more on-site irrigation reservoirs. We are also delivering long-term change in the water industry to reduce leaks and deliver nine new reservoirs and water transfer schemes to secure supplies.

“As we move through this period of drought, I expect water companies to take every available step to minimise leakage and support customers in using water wisely. I also want to thank people for following the restrictions, where in place, as they are an important tool to safeguard essential water supplies and protect the environment.”

View 20 Images Firefighters continue to battle a blaze at the Holme Fen Nature Reserve (Image: Getty Images)

‌



The group heard how the current drought now means there have been three in the past five years – 2022, 2025 and now 2026. After the meeting, the Government said it was stepping up its drought response and is considering ways to give more support to farmers.

It pointed out that England is not alone in facing drought as mainland Europe is also struggling with heatwaves and dry weather. It also said our river flows continue to decline, with only 14% classed as at normal levels. 22% are exceptionally low, including the Avon, Wye, Ely Ouse and Exe.

View 20 Images Dried out ground of Maiden Castle Iron Age hillfort in Dorchester (Image: Getty Images)

Reservoir levels have fallen to 69% - 11.6% lower than to be expected for this time of year. England reservoir storage fell 16% during July, the greatest reduction in raw storage in July for at least 30 years. Livestock farmers are beginning to feed winter forage stocks earlier than normal due to poor grass growth. The lack of adequate feed is expected to result in decreased milk volumes.

‌



View 20 Images The pitch at Radnage Recreation Ground, home of Radnage Raiders FC, Radnage, Buckinghamshire (Image: Jonathan Brady/PA Wire)

NFU Deputy President Paul Tompkins said: “With no meaningful rain forecast in the coming weeks, the situation facing farmers and growers is increasingly concerning. Many farmers have completed the earliest harvest on record, with poor yields in key crops reported in some areas of the country. Livestock and dairy farmers are already using winter feed because grass has stopped growing, while growers are working hard to keep fruit and vegetables watered, but many are struggling to access the water they need.

View 20 Images Major heathland blaze in the New Forest near Ringwood in Hampshire (Image: Forestry England/PA Wire)

“To help farmers and growers now, we need to see a risk register for vulnerable businesses and a more responsive abstraction licensing system. Longer term, a consistent and positive planning approach to reservoirs, further rounds of the Water Management Grant and targeted investment in climate adaptation will be vital to build farming's resilience to extreme weather.

‌



View 20 Images South London has turned orange after the lack of rain (Image: Jordan Pettitt/PA Wire)

“Water plays a crucial role in food security and the resilience of our nation. By treating water for food as a strategic priority, government can work with farmers to protect crops, livestock businesses, and the UK’s long-term food security.”

View 20 Images Hampshire and IOW Fire and Rescue Service delpoyed a large water pipe from lakes within the New Forest towards the scene of a wildfire (Image: FACEBOOK)

They told how wildlife and fishing has also been suffering in the drought.

‌



Mark Owen, Head of Fisheries at the Angling Trust, said: “Warmer water holds less dissolved oxygen, putting fish under severe stress that can quickly become life-threatening.

View 20 Images An explosion has set fire to fields and commercial buildings in Hertfordshire (Image: Kevin Bownes / SWNS)

“Anglers often spot problems first and play an important role raising the alarm when fish are in distress. This summer, we have seen an increasing number of incidents linked to prolonged hot, dry weather and exceptionally low river flows. More frequent droughts and rising water temperatures are placing even greater pressure on rivers, making it increasingly difficult for fish and other wildlife to survive unless we build greater resilience into our freshwater environment.

View 20 Images Low water levels reveal the lakebed at Hanningfield Reservoir, Essex (Image: NEIL HALL/EPA/Shutterstock)

‌



“If you see fish gasping at the surface, stranded in isolated pools or large numbers showing signs of distress, report it immediately to the Environment Agency's 24-hour incident hotline on 0800 80 70 60. Early reports from anglers and other river users can make all the difference, giving fisheries teams the best chance of saving fish before it's too late."

View 20 Images A blaze near Llangynidr Reservoir, Ebbw Vale in Blaenau Gwent started on Saturday (Image: SWFRS / SWNS)

Head of Environment and Energy at the Met Office, Sarah Davies, said: "July 2026 was one of the most remarkable months in the UK's climate record. England and Wales both recorded their driest and sunniest July on record, together with periods of exceptionally high temperatures. These conditions have significantly increased pressure on water resources in some parts of the country and contributed to the ongoing drought concerns.

View 20 Images Hanningfield reservoir's stocks are incredibly low (Image: NEIL HALL/EPA/Shutterstock)

‌



"Looking ahead, forecasts for the remainder of August and into September suggest a good deal of dry weather is expected, mixed with some unsettled spells. While some areas may see useful rainfall at times, there is currently no strong signal for a sustained period of widespread rainfall, with below average rainfall more likely than above-average for the period as a whole.

"The Met Office will continue to work closely with partners through the National Drought Group, providing forecasts and climate intelligence to support planning and decision-making as conditions evolve."

View 20 Images More than half of England being declared in a drought (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Nicci Russell, CEO at Waterwise, said: “The experts are telling us that these extraordinary climate emergency impacts we're seeing in real time, right in front of our eyes, are not random one-off events. It's entirely reasonable that at this time, we only use water for essential purposes. None of us can live without water - and society, the economy and the environment can't function without it.

‌



View 20 Images The dried and cracked bed of the depleted Hollow Pond and Leyton flats near Wanstead, east London (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

“We all have a role to play in making sure there's enough water to go round - and there are lots of simple things we can all do at home and at work to help close the gap between the water we need, and the water we have. Turn that hosepipe off! Step away from the sprinkler! Let your lawn go golden and your car go dirty. Knock a minute off your shower time - imagine if everyone in England and Wales did that, saving 15 litres of water every time, and you can see how small actions by each of us make a real difference.

“We all need to save water - of course there is work to do for the water companies and governments, and big business, but we all need to step up.”

View 20 Images Smoke from the wildfire at Llangynidr reservoir near Crickhowell spreads across the landscape (Image: John Myers)

‌



Eight water companies have introduced Temporary Use Bans (TUBs), in some or all of their areas, impacting over 27 million customers. They are: Affinity Water, Anglian Water, Cambridge Water, Essex & Suffolk Water, Southern Water, South East Water, Thames Water and South West Water.

Southern Water has applied for two Drought Orders. The first is to maintain normal abstraction rates from the River Test even during low flows and the second is for a non-essential use ban. These are both under consideration by Defra.

The National Drought Group recommended water companies submit drought permits early to allow them to refill reservoirs as early as possible.

News.title: Bomb squad races to Edinburgh street as evacuation ordered over 'suspicious item'
News.content:
Bomb squad races to Edinburgh street as evacuation ordered over 'suspicious item'

A bomb squad has been called to a potentially 'suspicious item' on Restalrig Ave between Loganlea Ave and Loganlea Drive in Edinburgh, with residents evacuated

View Image Police have put a cordon in place at the scene (Image: Edinburgh Live)

Residents have been evacuated from an Edinburgh street with a bomb squad called over a potentially "suspicious item".

‌



Emergency services raced to the incident on Restalrig Ave between Loganlea Ave and Loganlea Drive, with the area now cordoned off by police.

‌



Dozens of officers are in attendance at Restalrig Avenue with locals telling of a 'road closed' sign being erected shortly before 3pm today.

‌



An eyewitness claimed officers spoke to residents telling them to leave their homes due to a package that had been found. Police can be seen standing at either end of the road to stop people from entering the street.

A statement from Police Scotland read: "Restalrig Ave is closed between Loganlea Ave and Loganlea Drive due to a report of a potentially suspicious item. Emergency services and Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) are in attendance.

"A cordon is in place as a precaution. The public is asked to avoid the area."

‌



The cordon is also causing travel disruption and a bus diversion is in place for the 25 service, reported EdinburghLive.

Lothian Buses said: "Due to a road closure buses are unable to serve Loganlea Drive and Restalrig Avenue and are instead diverted via Craigentinny Avenue, Portobello Road, Wakefield Avenue and terminating on Craigentinny Road until further notice."

Meanwhile, a suspected unexploded World War Two bomb was found at a quarry in Staffordshire last week.

‌



Residents had to be evacuated near the site on Walton Lane, Barton-under-Needwood last Thursday evening. Trains running between Tamworth and Burton-on-Trent were also cancelled or delayed while the bomb was investigated, National Rail said.

The bomb was safely detonated in a planned controlled explosion, said Staffordshire Police.

A spokesperson said: "A controlled explosion has been carried out by specialists from Explosive Ordnance Disposal on the suspected WW2 bomb at a quarry in the Barton-under-Needwood area this evening.

Article continues below

"The cordon has been reduced from 900m to 200m, which will be removed fully this evening. A small number of residents who had been evacuated are returning to their properties. The A38, and other closed roads, will be re-opened to traffic."

News.title: King donates entire field of wheat to struggling straw hat maker amid national shortage
News.content:
King donates entire field of wheat to struggling straw hat maker amid national shortage

Emily Hurst, who specialises in making straw hats for women, has received an incredible donation from the King after telling him her business was struggling

View 4 Images King Charles has helped a struggling artist in the wake of a straw shortage (Image: Getty Images)

King Charles has donated an entire field of wheat on the Sandringham estate to a hat maker amid a national shortage of straw.

‌



Emily Hurst, a milliner who specialises in crafting and designing high-end straw hats for women and is preparing for the fifth heatwave of the summer, has been struggling to source heritage straw for her creations.

‌



The designer, who trained at the King's country retreat of Highgrove, spoke to Charles and told him she was struggling to obtain Maris Widgeon - a traditional British wheat variety prized by milliners - due to poor harvests and extreme weather conditions.

‌



Meghan Markle wears Diana's earrings in candid selfie of her and Prince Harry at glitzy party READ MORE :

View 4 Images Milliner Emily Hurst with her straw hat creations (Image: PA)

After hearing about her struggle, the monarch donated an entire field of the crop to Emily from the Sandringham estate - the private country estate of the King and Queen - in a moment she described as ‘surreal’.

Speaking on BBC Radio 4, Ms Hurst said: “We’ve got a whole field’s worth here, I could potentially create hundreds of hats from this. It’s quite hard to imagine if I’m honest, it’s still quite surreal, it’s still sinking in.”

‌



In 2025, Ms Hurst became the first recipient of a £10,000 bursary, awarded by Ascot Racecourse to a Chanel and King’s Foundation fellowship student. She graduated from the 35-week course, which is based at the King’s Highgrove Gardens in Gloucestershire, having trained across a range of materials and using historic machines.

She said at the time: “I’m incredibly grateful to receive this bursary from Ascot, which will make a vital difference as I begin my professional journey. It’s a huge honour to have my work recognised in this way and I owe so much to my time on the Chanel and King’s Foundation Millinery Fellowship.

View 4 Images King Charles battling the heat at a reception at St James' Palace earlier in summer (Image: Getty Images)

‌



“Straw is an extraordinary and often overlooked material with deep cultural significance and an exciting future in modern fashion. I’m passionate about helping this heritage craft not only survive, but thrive again.”

Emily’s hats have since been available to buy at the Highgrove shop, including a £475 straw visor, with proceeds of the sales going to the King’s Foundation. She has also gone on to work with luxury ateliers. The hat designer is just one of millions of people affected by the UK’s brutal summer, with Brits preparing for more extreme temperatures set to arrive later this week.

It also comes as farmers are facing their worst harvest on record for 2026 after several months of little rain, with estimates that the grain harvest could shrink by 2.5 million tons, which could cost farmers nearly £400 million, according to some forecasts.

‌



The ongoing heat has also caused unprecedented wildfires in the UK, with fires emerging across the south of England. A fire broke out in the New Forest near Bolderwood, Hampshire, yesterday, with motorists being told by police to abandon their cars if they "want to live".

View 4 Images Another heatwave is on the horizon for this week as blazes continue across the country (Image: Ian West/PA Wire)

‌



The blaze is feared to have caused decades-long damage to protected heathland that is home to wild ponies, deer, rare birds and insects. The UK faces its fifth heatwave of the year this week as weather forecasts suggest temperatures could peak as high as 39C.

Met Office forecasters are considering issuing amber or red extreme heat warnings ahead of what could be the hottest day of the year on Thursday. The current temperature record for 2026 stands at 37.7C, which came on June 26 in Lingwood, Norfolk.

Temperatures are expected to peak at 29C today and 30C tomorrow, before surging into the mid-30s from Wednesday. The GFS model shows highs of 36C are on the cards in western parts of England on Wednesday.
