Sports.title: 'If we maximise everything, it's achievable': TOM CLEVERLEY on Plymouth's promotion charge, working 14-hour days and asking old friend Michael Carrick for help with signings
Sports.content:
'If we maximise everything, it's achievable': TOM CLEVERLEY on Plymouth's promotion charge, working 14-hour days and asking old friend Michael Carrick for help with signings

Unlock more of the best of our journalism with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight and the writers you love every day

As a man who sang Stand By Me at his Aston Villa initiation in 2014, Tom Cleverley is grateful that Plymouth Argyle got the message more than a decade on.

He is preparing for a second campaign in charge of a club with which he has hit the depths – they were bottom of League One in late November – and very nearly the heights. That they only missed out on the play-offs in the dying minutes of last season is testament to his inspiration and resilience. That he was still in charge was down to the club's patience.

The target is still promotion this time around, but the Pilgrims' progress won't come easy when their competition includes Leicester City and Sheffield Wednesday. They have already sold star striker Lorent Tolaj for £4million to Bristol City and Cleverley will only get to spend some of that on replacing him; Will Evans has signed for an undisclosed fee from Mansfield.

But Cleverley knows his side can compete with the best in the division. Only Lincoln City had a better record in the third tier since the start of 2026 and the 36-year-old former Manchester United, England and Watford midfielder is more prepared than he was 12 months ago.

'I’ve learned a lot,' he tells Daily Mail Sport. 'The biggest thing is my knowledge of League One. I researched every player we were playing against but until you’ve experienced the heat of the battle, it’s tough to know how to be at your most effective. You never stop learning. You want to be in the training ground 14 hours a day but you quickly learn that's got a short shelf life.

'I've got to grips with what the league takes. I know the strengths and weaknesses of my players. If we maximise every department of the football club, promotion is achievable.

Tom Cleverley is preparing for his second campaign in charge of Plymouth Argyle

He has struck up a strong relationship with supporters after a fantastic run of form in 2026

'I'm very detailed. Which side you press someone off, to when you’re pressing, are you checking your shoulders? All these things, really tactical. Be detailed to give your players an edge, but don't overload them.

'I wouldn’t pigeonhole myself into one style of tactical identity. I’m someone who believes in getting the best out of the players you’ve got, identifying their strengths and weaknesses, and creating a gameplan.'

Cleverley cites Unai Emery as one manager he admires for his adaptability, detail and record of improving players. In the Football League, when bigger clubs regularly poach players, being able to work with what you've got is vital.

He has also called in a few favours from an old Manchester United team-mate, with whom he won a Premier League title in 2013. Michael Carrick let Plymouth train at United's Carrington base last season before their trip to Stockport County.

'We’ve used Carrington, so I see Jonny Evans and Michael there,' Cleverley says. 'We’re good friends away from football, so we've had real good conversations about potential loans. Every young English coach will be rooting for him this year.'

Cleverley enjoys listening to Oasis, Blossoms and Courteeners, all bands from his old city. He'll certainly need some music for the season ahead, when he will spend more than £12,000 on coach trips with his squad for away days from Devon.

Plymouth were surprisingly strong on the road last campaign. They earned 39 points on their travels (one fewer than when they won the title in 2022-23), winning 12 games.

Typically, they travel the morning before a match and train at a club's facilities nearby, before getting home as late as 4am on the night of the game. Players then get a day and a half off to recuperate.

'I've got to grips with what the league takes. I know the strengths and weaknesses of my players. If we maximise every department of the football club, promotion is achievable'

Cleverley (left) with Michael Carrick (right) in the 2012-13 season, when they won the Premier League together in Sir Alex Ferguson's final season in charge

'You want to be in the training ground 14 hours a day but you quickly learn that's got a short shelf life'

'The travelling isn't mentioned as much internally as it is externally!' says Cleverley. 'We try to recruit the right profile of player and character that doesn’t moan about small things.

'We know what we’re signing up for here. We do have the challenge of miles on the clock. It’s not a negative or an excuse, it’s a challenge, and we come across challenges big or small every day.'

After being the first person in and last person out every day, Cleverley is feeling 'refreshed' after a few weeks back home in Manchester and on holiday in North Wales this summer. He's also been to St George's Park to work on his English Pro Licence.

His more than 400 games as a player and manager have contained immense highs and lows. Roy Hodgson once compared him to Cesc Fabregas and he picked up 13 caps for England. He was also relegated with Watford and was the subject of a fan petition to exclude him from the 2014 World Cup, which hit the then 24-year-old hard.

All of that has given him a certain detachment when it comes to the struggles of football. In the pressure cooker of last October and November, when he looked on the brink of losing his job, Cleverley didn't flinch.

'It wasn’t as difficult as some people might have thought,' he says. 'I suffered a very difficult time in my playing career when I was 23, 24, that gave you a numbness and a thickness of skin in your life.

'It’s difficult not seeing your team win because you don’t sacrifice your life for poor performances or results. That’s hard. You sacrifice so much to see no outcome. But the abuse, I can take that, I've been in football long enough. I enjoy being the person to give direction out of those moments.'

Cleverley's emotional stability is just as well, because he intends to be in this for the long haul. He has embraced the Plymouth community and sees his job as a project.

Roy Hodgson once compared Cleverley (right) to Cesc Fabregas (centre)

He won 13 caps for England and represented Team GB at the London 2012 Olympics

Cleverley's emotional stability is just as well, because he intends to be in this for the long haul. He has embraced the Plymouth community and sees his job as a project

After arriving in Devon, Daily Mail Sport has learned, he went on a local history tour to understand the city. As we speak, he is celebrating a £65,000 grant from Sky Bet for Plymouth to run a programme helping women through their perimenopause and menopause.

'We’re a club that really does walk the walk when we say we’re a community club and a family club,' he says. 'We have days with open training, Christmas carols, whatever it may be, we try to engage and give back to our loyal supporters.

'I’m certainly passionate, intense, players will call me quite detailed. I want to create an energy within the stadium. That’s a real important connection. I’m excited to be on this journey.'

Tom Cleverley was speaking after Plymouth Argyle received a £65,000 grant from the Sky Bet EFL Building Foundations Fund to launch a new programme supporting women through perimenopause and menopause.

Sports.title: Derby's Saudi takeover COLLAPSES: Championship club now 'off the market' after Turki Alalshikh's group dramatically pulled out despite Football Regulator and EFL approval
Sports.content:
Derby County's proposed Saudi takeover has collapsed after new investors dramatically pulled the plug, despite winning approval from the Football Regulator and the EFL.

Lion Sport, headed by Saudi boxing supremo Turki Alalshikh, were on the cusp of completing the takeover before the Championship club announced on Monday that the proposed new ownership has had a change of heart.

The Rams have confirmed they are no longer on the market, with the EFL season kicking off this weekend.

'The club can confirm discussions with Lion Sport to buy a controlling interest in Derby County will no longer proceed,' the second-tier outfit said in a statement posted on X.

Turki Alalshikh's Lion Sport group has pulled out of taking over Derby County Football Club

A takeover had been approved by the EFL and Football Regulator but will no longer happen

'The purchase process had been sanctioned by both the Independent Football Regulator and the EFL, notification of which the club received last week.

'However, today the club received notice that Lion Sport no longer wanted to continue with the purchase.

'For the benefit of any doubt, the club is now off the market and will continue to operate under the loyal, committed and unwavering support of Clowes Developments.

'Our preparations continue for the new EFL season, beginning against Charlton Athletic on Saturday. The club will offer no further comment.'

Turki Alalshikh later posted his own statement to X, saying: 'I would like to thank everyone at Derby County Football Club, and everyone involved in this process for all their hard work over the past few months.

'We understood that the IFR process takes time and fully respects the importance of that, but unfortunately with the season already started, it would leave us with no time to prepare the team or the club for the season ahead.

'After careful consideration, we don't feel it is right to proceed at this time without the necessary preparation in place, but we will remain in conversation with the club and see what is possible in the future.

'I personally wish the team and club every success for the season ahead.'

More to follow.

Sports.title: 'We wanted Marco to stay - we had the contract ready. We were taken aback': Fulham vice-chairman TONY KHAN on Silva's exit, a 'bright future' under Alvaro Arbeloa, signing Real Madrid's young stars and the 'danger' he saved the club from
Sports.content:
This summer of change after five years of stability was not entirely what Tony Khan anticipated as Fulham negotiated the finer details of a new contract for Marco Silva.

They thought the deal was done and were poised, ready to confirm Silva had agreed to extend his time at Craven Cottage when Benfica swooped in and lured him back to Portugal.

After a decade in office, Khan is conditioned to expect the unexpected. The 43-year-old son of Fulham's billionaire owner Shahid Khan has weathered the nepotism jibes and matured into the role of vice-chairman and director of football operations. He has, by his own admission, developed a thicker skin to accompany his deeper understanding of English football and recruitment successes.

There are subtle differences from the world of US sport, where he holds a key executive position at the Jacksonville Jaguars, his father's other big sporting interest in the NFL, and All Elite Wrestling, his own personal creation which he founded and fronts.

At Fulham, Khan the younger runs the club's football business in a triumvirate with chief executive Alistair Mackintosh and the head coach – Silva for the last five years and now former Real Madrid boss Alvaro Arbeloa.

'After working together for several years with this consistent run of results, we wanted Marco to stay,' Khan tells Daily Mail Sport by way of explanation. 'We had very positive talks. We all get along very well. It's a very positive friendship between Marco, myself and my dad. We're all good friends.

Tony Khan (left), the 43-year-old son of Fulham's billionaire owner Shahid (right) has weathered nepotism jibes and matured into the role of vice-chairman and director of football operations

His latest move was getting former Real Madrid interim boss Alvaro Arbeloa (centre) to come to west London

'I had started planning for the next season and was building scouting bulletins and organising our plans. Marco came in and fully negotiated the contract. We all expected him to sign it and then were taken aback when that wasn't what happened.

'But I completely understand the decision he made to go home and work at a club of that magnitude, with the opportunity to live in his own house with his family every night. Those things made a lot of sense.'

Benfica moved for out-of-contract Silva after Jose Mourinho left them for a second spell at Real Madrid, two deals oiled by Jorge Mendes, who is the agent of both managers.

Fulham closed the Lisbon-Madrid-London triangle by appointing former Liverpool, Real, West Ham and Spain right back Arbeloa, who ended last season in interim charge of Real following Xabi Alonso's sacking, after his coaching impressed in the academy and with the reserves.

'I'm very grateful to Marco,' says Khan. 'I consider him an important friend and a very important person in the history of the club. I know Alvaro really respects the job Marco did, the core we all built and Marco led, coached and strengthened.

'That's part of what made this an attractive opportunity for Alvaro. It is a very important summer for Fulham. It's a challenge when somebody moves on after that length of time and you move to the next step for the club. But Alvaro joins us at a perfect time. It's a very exciting time.'

Silva was the only candidate interviewed five years ago, when he replaced Scott Parker after relegation to the Championship. He was identified as a perfect fit and proved to be a terrific success. Khan says: 'My father has been at the Jacksonville Jaguars for 15 years and now over 13 years at Fulham, and Marco has had the longest tenure of any coach at either club.'

Silva led Fulham to promotion in his first season, then established the club in the Premier League by finishing 10th, 13th, 11th and 11th. They reached a League Cup semi-final in 2024 and two FA Cup quarter-finals during his tenure.

Marco Silva led Fulham to promotion in his first season, then established the club in the Premier League by finishing 10th, 13th, 11th and 11th

Arbeloa ended last season in interim charge of Real following Xabi Alonso's sacking, after his coaching impressed in the academy and with the reserves

This summer they considered and spoke to several candidates before settling on 43-year-old Arbeloa, undeterred by his limited experience coaching on the front line.

'Everybody agreed Alvaro was the most exciting, fresh, dynamic and intelligent person we connected with,' says Khan. 'And the person we thought would connect with our players and give Fulham the best opportunity going forward. That's why we hired him.

'He worked with Real Madrid's first team and their young players and has a lot of football experience.'

Arbeloa spent two years at Liverpool and a year at West Ham in a playing career decorated by two Champions League wins at Real Madrid, as well as a World Cup and two Euros wins with Spain.

'He was a great player,' says Khan. 'He knows the Premier League, and his experiences are different to the experiences we have here. Alvaro brings a fresh perspective with his energy, ideas and connections. He is hard working, driven for success. There's a very bright future with him here for all of us.'

Arbeloa's connections have already secured the services of Gonzalo Garcia and Cesar Palacios, talented youngsters from Real Madrid for a combined fee of £42.5million.

The bulk of that is for Garcia, a 22-year-old forward who made 30 La Liga appearances for Real last season and won his first Spain cap in June. Palacios is a 21-year-old attacking midfielder whom Arbeloa describes as 'a magician' that will get Fulham fans out of their seats.

How quickly they settle will determine how far they go towards replacing Raul Jimenez and Harry Wilson, Fulham's two top scorers in the Premier League last season who both left this summer at the end of their contracts.

Arbeloa (pictured playing against Fulham in 2008) made 98 appearances for Liverpool in a two-and-a-half-year spell

Gonzalo Garcia has arrived with Arbeloa from Real, having scored 13 times in 51 senior games for the club he joined as a 10-year-old

And so has Cesar Palacios, a midfielder who played seven times for Madrid and has represented Spain at Under-20 level

Jimenez, who scored nine, has returned to Wolverhampton Wanderers. Wilson, who scored ten (and enough screamers for his own Goal of the Season competition), left for Leeds after rejecting a new contract.

'Leeds were very interested in Harry Wilson late in the window last summer,' says Khan. 'It was such a large amount of money that it was something we had to look at and talk about, but the club made a very important decision keeping him at Fulham.

'He scored some very important goals in key situations and has been a strong player through five excellent years. I was hoping he would stay. Leeds got a fantastic player. He's been very well compensated, which he deserves, and I wish Harry the absolute best in everything he does unless it's against Fulham.'

Khan took control of Fulham's transfers in the summer of 2016 after finishing 20th in the Championship, the club's lowest finish since promotion to the second tier under Kevin Keegan in 1999.

'I saw the danger of the road the club were on,' he says. 'I thought it needed a complete upheaval. I approached my dad and said I really think I should take over the transfers and loans.

'I was 33 years old and believed the team could do much better. A few years ago, I never would've thought I'd be here saying this. In 2013 [when Khan paid £150million to buy the club from Mohamed Al Fayed] I never would've thought I'd say it.

'We kept the key players and brought in a completely new squad. The vast majority were new players. That team finished sixth and lost in the play-offs and the next year we got promoted after some important moves in the next couple of windows including Aleksandar Mitrovic on loan from Newcastle.'

Mitrovic – signed for £27million after a successful loan and sold for £50million to Al Hilal in Saudi Arabia in 2023 after scoring 111 goals in five-and-a-half years at Fulham – must rank among the best deals of Khan's time in office. His favourite though might be the return of Ryan Sessegnon, five years after a £25million move to Tottenham which brought the popular young left back nothing but bad luck with injuries.

Fulham's top two goalscorers last season, Raul Jimenez (left) and Harry Wilson (right), both left the club this summer when their contracts ended

Aleksandar Mitrovic (right) - signed for £27m and sold for £50m to Al Hilal in Saudi Arabia in 2023 after scoring 111 goals - must rank among the best deals of Khan's time in office

'When I first started working in the office, Ryan was a talented player coming through the academy and starting to train with the first team,' recalls Khan. 'I rode five hours in the car to see his first league match [at the age of 16] against Leeds.

'Incredibly, that was 10 years ago this month. To have him back and part of the team now is special, and he's still a young guy with a great career in front of him at Fulham.'

Despite losing Jimenez, Wilson and Issa Diop, sold to Ipswich for £8.5million, Fulham maintain the bones of a strong, settled and experienced team, which Khan expects to be boosted by the progress of talented youngsters.

Not only Garcia and Palacios, and wingers Oscar Bobb and Kevin, both 23, but also Jonah Kusi-Asare, 19, a Swedish striker signed for £5million after a year on loan from Bayern Munich and Josh King, also 19, who emerged last season from the club's prolific academy.

Fulham remain active in the transfer market. There has been genuine interest in 19-year-old Thiago Pitarch, another of Real Madrid's prized young players, whom Arbeloa coached in the youth teams and then gave him his senior debut in February against, you guessed it, Benfica. Signing Pitarch would be an audacious coup for Arbeloa although it appears unlikely.

They are close to completing the £30million signing of Southampton's Northern Ireland international midfielder Shea Charles, who came through Manchester City's academy and scored the late goal that knocked Arsenal out of last season's FA Cup.

'I'm very happy with what the club has achieved in recent years,' says Khan. 'Four years ago, everyone would have considered this to be very successful.

'Now it's a time to try new things but to keep many of these players who've been important in the run of success and stability at Fulham.

Thiago Pitarch (right) who was given his senior Real debut by Arbeloa, is another young talent on Fulham's radar this summer

They are close to completing a £30million deal for Southampton's Shea Charles (centre), who knocked Arsenal out of last season's FA Cup

'I'm very happy with what the club has achieved in recent years,' says Khan. 'Four years ago, everyone would have considered this to be very successful'

'We've had new milestones under Marco, the furthest the club has gone in the League Cup, the most points ever in a Premier League campaign (54 in 2024-25).

'I hope we can build on that. We have a strong core with players in their prime who we know can play together and exciting young players who can come in and compete with a young coach.

'Hopefully there's new milestones to hit in the league and cup, but I want to keep the club in a stable position in the Premier League.'

Sports.title: Amazon founder and billionaire Jeff Bezos closes in on deal to buy minority stake in Liverpool as consortium's £1.35billion investment nears approval
Sports.content:
Amazon founder and billionaire Jeff Bezos is closing in on a deal to buy a minority stake in Liverpool.

Bezos is part of a billionaire boys' club featuring the owner of Facebook and the son-in-law of an Indian steel magnate, with the consortium set to purchase a share of the Premier League giants that equates to around 30 per cent.

Daily Mail Sport reported three weeks ago that a group led by Amit Bhatia, the former co-owner of Championship side Queens Park Rangers, were serious and confident of buying that percentage of the club for roughly £1.35billion from Liverpool's American owners Fenway Sports Group (FSG).

And now sources indicate the process is ticking along nicely, with suggestions it could be rubber-stamped in the next week.

Bezos, who has an estimated net worth of £207.4billion, per Forbes, is the most notable name involved in the deal alongside Mark Zuckerberg’s classmate and Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin, valued at £24.5bn.

Bhatia will lead the bid. He stepped down after nearly two decades as QPR supremo last month – he has a stand named after him at Loftus Road – and he is the son-in-law of steel tycoon Lakshmi Mittal, who is the world’s 65th-richest man with £24.8bn to his name.

Amazon founder Jeff Bezos is part of a group set to buy a minority stake in Liverpool

John W Henry, the principal chair of Fenway Sports Group, who own Liverpool, has always been eager for additional investment while still being keen to hold the majority stake

It is understood the 46-year-old British-Indian business leader Bhatia has also entrusted the help of a senior PR executive who previously worked for Manchester United and King Charles when he was the Prince of Wales.

Bezos' net worth ranks him as the third-richest man in the world, and while he is no longer the CEO of Amazon, he retains the title of executive chairman.

He has never previously invested in sport, although he was interested in buying the current Super Bowl winners Seattle Seahawks and fellow NFL team Washington Commanders before pulling out.

Liverpool are already one of 11 Premier League clubs under American ownership, which includes fellow Big Six teams Arsenal, Chelsea and Manchester United.

Arsenal owner Stan Kroenke made his money in commercial real estate development by developing a strategic business relationship with American supermarket Walmart, with his wife Ann Walton the daughter of Bud Walton, who co-founded the chain. He also has a significant sports and land empire.

Meanwhile, Chelsea are owned by a consortium named Blue Co, which is co-led by Clearlake Capital, an LA-based private equity firm, and American businessman Todd Boehly.

Manchester United are owned by the Glazer Family, who are from the US and valued at around £8.87bn, while Sheikh Mansour, a member of the ruling family of Abu Dhabi and the vice-president of the UAE, is Man City's majority owner.

Newcastle United were taken over in 2021 by a consortium of the Saudi Public Investment Fund.

In terms of what a potential Bezos takeover means for Liverpool, there are warnings to fans getting excited about the mega-money set to come in: the club itself won’t have direct access to an infinite supply of cash, as the funds will go to FSG and not the team.

The Premier League has recently introduced a modern version of financial fair play with the ‘squad cost ratio’ rules which state that clubs can only spend a set percentage of its football-related revenue and profit/loss from player sales.

It is around 85 per cent but can be 70 per cent for those competing in Europe, as Liverpool often is.

However, if the club was looking to borrow money at a future date, they will be in a position to do so on an interest-free basis which can only benefit cash flow. Bezos and Saverin’s names help with commercial deals.

Some fans are also worried that this is a sign of FSG slowly selling up, with principal owner John W Henry now 76. FSG sources say this is the opposite and insist this is another way the owner is looking to further position the club for success.

The Boston-based owners, with Mike Gordon more hands-on again now Michael Edwards has departed, will still make the day-to-day decisions despite selling off 30 per cent of the club.

When approached for comment, FSG referred to an earlier statement which said Bhatia and a consortium had expressed interest in an investment. Bezos was also approached.

MEET THE KEY PLAYERS

JEFF BEZOS

Bezos is the third-richest man in the world, according to Forbes. In 1994, he read that web usage was growing at a rate of 2,300 per cent a year and wanted to open an online book store, so set one up in his garage in Seattle alongside his then wife Mackenzie Scott.

He changed the name from Cadabra to Amazon after the South American river as, at the time, website listings were alphabetised so an ‘A’ listing would be near the top. They slowly started selling more products and are now one of the most recognisable companies in the world.

Bezos is no longer the CEO of Amazon but retains the title of executive chairman. He is also the owner of the Washington Post and founder of Blue Origin which competes with Elon Musk in the modern-day space race. He flew to space in 2021.

The 62-year-old has dabbled in the idea of sports investment before but this time appears to be different. He was interested in buying the current Super Bowl winners Seattle Seahawks and fellow NFL team Washington Commanders but pulled out.

He married former American journalist Lauren Sanchez last year.

Bezos has dabbled with the idea of sports ownership in the past but this time appears to be different

EDUARDO SAVERIN

Saverin was born in Brazil with Romanian heritage. He moved to Miami at age 13 and attended Harvard University. He became friends with fellow undergraduate Mark Zuckerberg and the pair wanted to set up a website for students to communicate, making a $1,000 investment each.

The site was originally named ‘The Facebook’ and soon grew to other universities, later anyone in the world aged 13 or older. It now has more than 3billion users and its parent company, Meta Platforms, has a market value of around £1.12trillion.

Saverin is played by Andrew Garfield in The Social Network film based on the book Accidental Billionaires about his rise at Facebook. Weeks before Facebook became a public company, he moved to Singapore and renounced his US citizenship.

The 44-year-old is now head of B Capital, a venture capital firm.

Eduardo Saverin was a co-founder of Facebook and is now head of venture capital firm B Capital

Amit Bhatia, the son in law of Lakshmi Mittal, previously worked for QPR for 19 years

AMIT BHATIA

Bhatia is a 46-year-old British-Indian with an investment banking background in sectors such as technology, media, property, real estate and health.

He formerly worked on Wall Street before founding a construction company aged 32, which has more than 5,000 UK employees. He won the young entrepreneur of the year award in 2013.

Bhatia married Vanisha Mittal in 2004 in a six-day wedding which the Guinness World Records recorded as the most-expensive ceremony of all time at £41m. Vanisha’s father is Lakshmi Mittal, the world’s 65th-richest man with £24.8bn as per Forbes.

Bhatia worked at QPR for 19 years and his company, AyBe Capital, owns shares in the cricket franchise London Spirit, former England cricketer Kevin Pietersen’s YouTube channel and an indoor golf league founded by Rory McIlroy.

The tycoon recently played a round of golf with basketball legend LeBron James and is regularly on the course with Indian cricketing icon Sachin Tendulkar.

Sports.title: Former Chelsea doctor Eva Carneiro aims thinly-veiled dig at Jose Mourinho on social media after his refusal to apologise over infamous touchline row in Netflix documentary
Sports.content:
Former Chelsea team doctor Dr Eva Carneiro has made a tongue-in-cheek jibe at Jose Mourinho in light of his comments about their infamous touchline row in a new documentary.

Mourinho avoided apologising to Carneiro when opening up about their infamous touchline row for the first time in over a decade in his new three-part Netflix docu-series titled MOURINHO, which is released on Tuesday.

The former Blues boss claimed he sees 'a lady doctor is the same as a man’s doctor' when addressing the incident which led to him agreeing a settlement with Carneiro after she took them to a tribunal in 2016 over claims that she was discriminated against by the manager.

And on the same day that Mourinho's quotes hit the headlines, Carneiro took to social media to make a light-hearted joke toward her former boss when announcing an exciting new chapter in her career.

Taking to X, Carneiro wrote that her announcement, which will be revealed in Autumn, was a 'Special One' before adding a winky face emoji.

'Bom Dia,' her post started. 'I have an announcement to make. A truly Special One.'

Bom Dia 😁⚽️!!!!!



I have an announcement to make.



A truly Special One 😉



A project close to my heart which I have been working on for years and is almost ready for launch.



Not an old set piece!



Watch this space. This autumn!!!! pic.twitter.com/kVXyNqJ3DD — Dr Eva Carneiro (@evacarneiro) August 10, 2026

Dr Eva Carneiro (left, pictured in 2015) has aimed a tongue-in-cheek dig at Joe Mourinho on social media

'A project close to my heart which I have been working on for years and is almost ready for launch. Not an old set piece! Watch this space. This autumn!!!!'

During a Premier League clash with Swansea City at the start of the 2015-16 season, Mourinho hit the roof when Carneiro and physio Jon Fearn went onto the pitch to treat Eden Hazard, who had gone down seemingly injured.

Dr Carneiro claimed that Mourinho sexually discriminated against her during his tirade and called her the 'daughter of a wh***' in his native Portuguese.

Back in 2015, Mourinho called her 'impulsive and naive' in his first public reaction to her decision to treat Hazard. She was then dropped from first-team duties and left the club just a month later.

Mourinho and Chelsea eventually agreed a settlement after Carneiro took them to a tribunal over claims that she was discriminated against by the manager, and constructively dismissed by the club.

But 11 years on, Mourinho believes he treated Carneiro in the same manner that he would treat any other doctor who made what he deemed as a mistake.

‘For me, a lady doctor is the same as a man’s doctor,' Mourinho said in the docu-series. 'So, as always, I use my vocabulary when I’m not happy.

'There are words in moments where the tension is very, very high. Normally, people with football culture, with football DNA, with football background, they go over it in one second. In that case, it was different.’

The 63-year-old has spoken up about the incident for the first time in over a decade in Netflix's new three-part docu-series MOURINHO

Hazard, who played under the now-63-year-old for two years, claimed 'it was nothing special' in the documentary, which is set to air on Tuesday, but 'with Jose everything is bigger'.

Footage shows that the Portuguese coach, who is now Real Madrid manager, shouted a whole host of expletives toward Carneiro and Fearn as they treated Hazard. He screamed phrases such as 'f*** off, man' and 'f*** you, man'.

'I’m not a doctor, but my eyes know when a player is injured, and they know when a player is not injured,' Mourinho said in the docu-series.

'I knew that he was not injured, but the doctors went to the pitch, and in that moment we were left with nine players.’

Hazard was forced to come off the pitch for a brief period, as is the rule when a player receives medical treatment, leaving Chelsea with nine men after Thibaut Courtois had been sent off.

Chelsea gave Dr Carneiro an unreserved apology, but Mourinho refused to say sorry and grinned as he left the tribunal.

A deal was done in a back corridor of the court and Chelsea then issued a statement saying it 'regretted the circumstances' which led to the former club doctor leaving and 'apologises unreservedly to her and her family for the distress caused'.

The terms of the settlement remain secret, but during the tribunal it was revealed that Chelsea had previously offered £1.2million to silence Carneiro.

Mourinho did not apologise after the incident or at the tribunal and there were no signs of an apology in the docu-series either.

Sports.title: Journey to Wembley: Daily Mail Sport's special 50th anniversary love letter to the FA Cup begins at 'Little Wembley', the home of Nelson FC - the ninth-tier side who were first EVER British team to win at Real Madrid
Sports.content:
Journey to Wembley: Daily Mail Sport's special 50th anniversary love letter to the FA Cup begins at 'Little Wembley', the home of Nelson FC - the ninth-tier side who were first EVER British team to win at Real Madrid

The ground at Nelson FC is called ‘Little Wembley’ and however resplendent the scene at its far grander namesake where the FA Cup final is played, 286 days and 600 or so games from now, it will do well to match the inestimable beauty of Saturday, when the arc of the old competition’s journey began once more.

The oasis of green in sun-starched east Lancashire has owed a lot to the club recently inviting the local fire service to carry out a practice drill which entailed spraying a lot of water on the pitch.

Limited supplies are also being piped a few hundred yards from Pendle Water, the river you cross to reach the ground, which once powered the local cotton mill, whose 200ft chimney and stone-built workers' cottages form the backdrop to one of the tournament’s 208 Preliminary Qualifying Round ties.

By 11am groundsman Trevor Stamworth is marking out the pitch, which locals took to calling 'Little Wembley' decades back because of its quality. Staff are setting up in the little bar area, where sepia images provide reminders of Nelson’s small but very significant part in football history – a 4-2 win over Real Madrid in 1923, during a tour of Spain, which made them the first British side to beat the club on their own turf.

A couple of deckchairs are set out in the front gardens of the workers’ cottages which form a warm-up area beside the pitch and Nelson manager Arron Ripley arrives at 1pm to lay out the team’s jerseys in the dressing room and hone a pre-match pep-talk which will include him reminding his players that only one in 3,400 people in Britain get to play in the FA Cup, so they should seize this day.

‘You’re just looking for the small details that might get through,’ 32-year-old Ripley reflects as we sit in the dug-out, watching his players warm-up. ‘We look to put detail on things in many ways. ‘A friend of mine who’s an analyst, puts together clips for the players and we’ve got GPS vests for every game. Our video recorder’s broken at the moment, but we usually watch games back.’

Daily Mail Sport headed to Nelson for the opening round of FA Cup ties

Nelson's 'Little Wembley' ground perfectly captures the magic of the FA Cup

Groundsman Trevor Stamworth marks out the pitch ahead of the match against Stockport Georgians

This bucolic scene on a peerless summer’s day creates the impression that there has not been a cloud in Nelson’s sky, though the reality is very different. The club has been the subject of various failed ownership experiments in recent times, leading to the club being in a state of financial peril, two years ago. The lumpy pitch always flooded, the team lost almost every week and they got barely 50 through the gate.

This coincided with local businessmen Chris Price, who is in the industrial cleaning business, learning that it might be for sale. He and a friend Stewart Fort, an engineering entrepreneur, bought it for the best part of £30,000, and have together set out on a mission to build a thriving community club and take it from tier 10 to the tier eight Northern Premier League whilst doing so.

The fruits of their labour and invention are all around the place, from the new club shop and stand, both built out of converted shipping containers, the smart, timber-built food facility and the small ‘Sponsors Lounge’, where Fort is helping lay out the knives and forks at midday. Price and Fort estimate they’ve put in £700,000, so far, with the £162,000 the FA has contributed a testament to the role the governing body is not always given full credit for.

From a near certain plunge to the West Lancashire League – a relegation spared by another club folding – Nelson won promotion to the North West Counties Premier Division last season and have started the new campaign with a win. The talk is of promotion again. But roads to recovery are neither easy nor linear in football.

Despite the co-owners laying out £32,000 on pitch drainage and £52,000 on new dressing rooms, seven of the ground’s eight floodlights have suddenly failed and contractors are currently battling to get new cables laid and get those lights back on.

Nelson aim to have 260 paying fans through the turnstiles each week

Co-owners Chris Price and Stewart Fort - who bought the club for just shy of £30,000, have turned Nelson into a local success story

Nelson's ground is called Little Wembley due to the high-quality playing surface

Fans enjoyed beers pitchside on a glorious day in east Lancashire

Here, in a microcosm, is evidence of why the FA Cup, which seems to have become a minor consideration for football’s great and good, matters so very much. Price and Fort are not petro-dollar billionaires or captains of finance and while they find the money for capital projects, the football side of things must fund itself. The more advertising boards they sell, the more resource will be available to Ripley to find players who, at this level, are paid an average of £100 a week.

‘Reaching the First Round Proper would earn us nearly £25,000 and that would make a massive difference to us,’ says Fort, as he reflects on some of the unglamorous work of the past few years here, including shifting 27 tons of muck out of the goalmouths to create the flat surface he looks out across. ‘The bigger picture is finding the 260 or so people we aim to get through the turnstiles every week. But this competition is everything for us.’

Ripley feels the significance of the income just as acutely, given that Nelson’s new ambition puts him under the same pressure that every manager knows - and contributed to the club parting company with him, just before Christmas 2024. ‘They sacked me after we’d lost five games but after my replacement didn’t get us promoted, they brought me back and last season we managed it,’ he says, ‘So yes, there’s all the pressure that comes at any ambitious club.’

That promotion has delivered Nelson to this, their first FA Cup appearance since 2017, since tier nine clubs are the lowest level who enter. ‘Over £1,000 winnings if we win today and that all goes into pot,’ Ripley says.

His managerial ethos entails being ‘very locally-driven’, with only one of his squad living more than half an hour from Nelson, and putting the time in to knowing who you’re up against. Ripley is very much part-time, too – a digital project manager with filling station operator EG – but he watched opponents Stockport Georgians beat Wythenshawe Town in the Midland League Premier a few days earlier.

The preparation shows. Nelson are stronger and quicker to the ball and, vitally, have Sefton Gonzales, a powerful and combative centre forward who works as a storeman, in their ranks. They lead through Lewis Brown, one of a Nelson midfield tandem who dominate the early stages, though no manner of opposition scouting can quell Stockport’s Lucas Berry, a former Salford City academy player who leaves the home team’s defence standing as he equalises.

Nelson's Sefton Gonzales celebrates scoring the winner with a back-flip

The victory for the hosts set up a meeting with eighth-tier Witton Albion in the next round of the competition

The club have spent £52,000 on new dressing rooms

A compelling game of combative and technically proficient football evolves on the Little Wembley baize, and it morphs into a question of which of the two outstanding goalscoring threats - Gonzales or Berry – will ultimately prevail. Berry spins and scores again after Luke Hepple has sent Nelson 2-1 up, but it is Gonzales who controls in close space and fires Nelson’s winner before sending his 6ft 2in frame through an improbable backflip.

The 3-2 scoreline blinks out from the new digital screen where they’re proud to display an image of the FA Cup and 87-year-old Eric Manning, whose meticulous, handwritten reports of the team’s games are typed up and published in the weekly Nelson Leader, can start reflecting on history repeating itself.

Next up, in the Preliminary Round, Nelson play eighth-tier Witton Albion, who they improbably beat on the way to a 3-2 loss at Port Vale in one of their most memorable Cup runs, in 1951. Manning missed the Port Vale game because his parents insisted on taking him on holiday.

Daily Mail Sport's Ian Herbert interviews Nelson manager Arron Ripley

We will be with Nelson at Witton, as the next in a series of pieces in which we take a club, any club, from the Preliminary Qualifying Round of the FA Cup, and follow them through the competition until they are defeated, then transferring allegiance to the victors…- and so on until Wembley.

The same project which Daily Mail football writer Brian James embarked on, exactly 50 years ago this month, for what became his legendary book, Journey to Wembley. We hope it will build a picture of the real football - our football – full of its hope, dreams, triumphs and setbacks.

Another of Nelson’s great historical claims is a 100% home record against Manchester United, given that they once beat them in the old Second Division and have never played them since.

‘We invited them over to play us and to see if we could extend that record,’ says Price. ’They’ve politely declined. We live in hope and they’d be so welcome!’ But a venture deep into the Cup would mean much more. ‘We want people to know what’s going on down here at our little place,’ Price says. ‘We believe that if we build, they will come.’

Sports.title: Ex-PGA Tour player Matt McQuillan dead at 45 as loved ones mourn tragic loss: 'Rest easy, Matty'
Sports.content:
Golf is mourning the loss of former PGA Tour player Matt McQuillan following his shock death at the age of just 45.

The Canadian, who was described as 'a respected golfer, devoted son, hilarious brother, and friend,' turned professional in 2003 after playing college golf at Oklahoma State and Georgia.

He later secured his place among golf's elite and went on to compete in 32 PGA Tour events, securing three top-10 finishes as a rookie.

But according to an obituary, he passed away on Wednesday surrounded by his family at a hospital in Ontario, Canada. No cause of death was listed.

'Whether on the course or in everyday life, he had a remarkable ability to bring people together, offering encouragement, laughter, and genuine friendship to everyone he met,' it read, per the Kingston Whig-Standard.

'His welcoming personality and unwavering kindness made him a beloved figure within Kingston's golfing community and beyond.'

Golf is mourning the loss of former PGA Tour player Matt McQuillan following his shock death

He passed away on Wednesday surrounded by his family at a hospital in Ontario, Canada

McQuillan's father, Mark, began teaching him how to swing a club at the age of 10 before he went on to reach the Canadian Tour and then the PGA Tour.

'Matt developed lifelong friendships while mentoring anyone who loved the game of golf,' his obituary continued.

'He will be deeply missed by many and his spirit, love and compassion will be remembered every day. Rest easy, Matty. We love you.'

Golf Canada added in a tribute that it 'joins the Canadian golf community in mourning the passing of Matt McQuillan... one of Canada's most promising young golfers in the late 1990s.'

According to the PGA Tour, the 45-year-old returned to his hometown of Kingston, Ontario, to teach golf, 'helping introduce and develop the next generation of Canadian golfers.'

McQuillan's best PGA Tour result came at the 2011 John Deere Classic when he shot a final-round 64 to finish in a tie for third behind winner Steve Stricker.

Sports.title: 9 new Premier League managers ranked as Andoni Iraola faces familiar Liverpool problem
Sports.content:
It's been a summer of upheaval in the Premier League, with nearly half of the 20 sides opting to change manager in the off-season.

Clubs at both ends of the spectrum have put their faith in a new boss in the hope that the 2026/27 season will bring success. Manchester City, Liverpool and Chelsea have all changed tack, albeit for differing reasons, with Enzo Maresca chosen to succeed Pep Guardiola, while Andoni Iraola and Xabi Alonso have walked in after frustrating campaigns under previous coaches.

Fulham, Nottingham Forest, Ipswich, Crystal Palace, Newcastle and Bournemouth also have fresh - but in some cases familiar - faces in the dugout. They know just how high the stakes are, especially at Forest, who burnt through four managers last season.

It is extremely unlikely that all nine new bosses will see their plans come to fruition in the coming months, so who will sink and who will swim? Here Mirror Football attempts to rank them in terms of which has the best chance of achieving their goals.

‌



9. Fulham - Alvaro Arbeloa

Marco Silva left Fulham this summer for Benfica having achieved one of the most boringly successful, under-the-radar stints in Premier League managerial history. After bringing Fulham up as champions in 2021/22, he embarked upon (depending on your viewpoint) mid-table security or mid-table mediocrity: 10th, 13th, 11th, 11th. In short, he did a good job but without pulling up trees.

It is into this context that Arbeloa walks, the Real Madrid cast-off attempting to establish himself. I would suggest that signing two other Real Madrid cast-offs, in Gonzalo Garcia and Cesar Palacios, may not have been the best way to try and move on from your past.

Harry Wilson, Fulham's stand-out player from last season, and Raul Jimenez, their experienced striker, have both left. We have no evidence yet that Arbeloa has the tactical nous to craft a new playing style, or the force of personality to create a team bond. I fear they are going to struggle.

View 7 Images Alvaro Arbeloa may struggle at Fulham (Image: Getty Images)

‌



8. Newcastle - Matthias Jaissle

You fear for Jaissle - and not because of anything he has done (yet). Newcastle have undergone a huge turnover this summer, selling Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimaraes, while also seeing Eddie Howe resign.

Howe was in situ for nearly five years and his exit was always going to cause instability. The fact his exit came alongside the departures of three key players means Newcastle are at risk of spiralling downwards after their 12th-place finish last season.

The Magpies' owners, Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, have promised a lot and Jaissle is their man, having been recruited from the relative obscurity of Al-Ahli. Just 38 years old, the German has landed an exciting job, but an extremely difficult one.

Their new signings this summer fall into the camp of 'plenty of potential' rather than 'proven performers'. There is still some time to add some players from the latter section, but reports that Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg has turned down the chance to join them suggests their transfer window woes could continue.

‌



View 7 Images Matthias Jaissle is the new man in charge at Newcastle (Image: 2026 Newcastle United)

7. Ipswich - Gary O'Neil

It's hard to judge O'Neil following a rollercoaster few years in management. But he won't have much time to settle in at Portman Road, having stepped into the breach following Kieran McKenna's surprise decision to walk away after leading the Tractor Boys to promotion.

O'Neil's star rose due to his spell at Bournemouth, fell after his time at Wolves - despite actually having a better win percentage - and then plateaued at Chelsea sister club Strasbourg. So is he one of the brightest English coaches in the game, or a middle-of-the-road one who has been over-promoted? We're about to get a better idea.

6. Liverpool - Andoni Iraola

View 7 Images Andoni Iraola has lots of problems to contend with (Image: Michael Miller/ISI Photos, ISI Photos via Getty Images)

‌



Iraola is obviously a brilliant coach and man-manager. His time at Bournemouth, in which he consistently improved the side, despite losing star after star to bigger clubs, earned him a shot at the big time. But pre-season has shown just how difficult the task is that he inherited from Arne Slot.

There are issues all over the pitch to address - from an ageing and injured central defence, through a central midfield which has lost its trademark high-energy pressing, to a misfiring (and extremely expensive) attack.

The job at Anfield is totally different to the one which the Spaniard became used to with the Cherries. He will have to manage egos, deal with heightened expectations, juggle the squad to cope with the Champions League, and - ultimately - win games straight away.

That will take time. This won't be a quick fix.

‌



5. Nottingham Forest - Oliver Glasner

Nuno Espirito Santo. Ange Postecoglou. Sean Dyche. Vitor Pereira. Forest went through all of them last season and still somehow managed to stay in the Premier League.

Glasner attracted plenty of interest when he announced he would leave Crystal Palace at the end of the season and eventually landed in Nottingham, where he will hope to buck the trend of notoriously impatient owner Evangelos Marinakis.

Glasner showed at Palace that he is an extremely shrewd operator with a clear playing style. He can drill players into his way of doing things. But, as we saw during his final months at Palace, he is not shy in voicing his frustrations when it comes to transfers. If he decides to take on Marinakis then it will only go one way.

View 7 Images Oliver Glasner has a completely different environment to deal with at Forest (Image: PA)

‌



4. Crystal Palace - Pierre Sage

The 47-year-old Frenchman arrived in south London after a seriously impressive one and only season with Lens, who he led to the Coupe de France final - the club's first since 1998 - and second place in Ligue 1.

The question is whether his success in France will translate into the Premier League with Palace following the successful reign of Glasner. Frank de Boer and Patrick Vieira are proof that it doesn't always work out like Glasner when taking a manager from abroad.

Sage worked in academy football for years before ascending to first-team football. He is a calm head and will take a methodical approach with Palace, which should mean a steady succession.

3. Chelsea - Xabi Alonso

View 7 Images Xabi Alonso has a huge squad to whittle down at Chelsea (Image: Yu Chun Christopher Wong/Getty Images)

‌



Alonso knows how hard it could be for him. "I had a view of Chelsea from the outside," he said this summer. "I could see the positives and my concerns so I addressed them."

The Spaniard has been handed more control than his predecessors, which is shown by his "manager" title, rather than "head coach". He failed at Real Madrid, but was extremely impressive at Bayer Leverkusen and has a ludicrously stacked squad with which to create his own identity at Chelsea.

While some managers have found the Blues' embarrassment of riches a hindrance, preferring a smaller squad, Alonso could be the man to tame it. If he can strike the right balance, maintaining squad harmony while honing in on those players who suit his style, they could be onto a winner.

2. Bournemouth - Marco Rose

Bournemouth's reputation for being a well-run club is fully deserved. Their recruitment team continually strike gold when scouring the market for young, talented and under-valued players. That - plus Iraola's coaching - has allowed them to continue to thrive despite selling those players on a few years later.

‌



Rose has worked at Borussia Dortmund and RB Leipzig, so has experience of 'bigger' clubs than Bournemouth. While he hasn't lasted long at either of the German giants, he has been hired due to his reputation as a coach who can get the best out of young players. Given their track record, I trust Bournemouth's judgement.

1. Manchester City - Enzo Maresca

View 7 Images Enzo Maresca has been groomed as Pep Guardiola's successor for some time

Pep Guardiola's successor has been groomed for many years for the role. Having worked under the City boss as a coach and soaked up his tactical philosophy, Maresca could hardly be more of a continuity pick.

The Italian left Chelsea under a cloud, but he has everything in place at City to succeed. Yes, following long-serving successful bosses is difficult, as David Moyes showed at Manchester United following Sir Alex Ferguson's departure. Maresca isn't walking into something unknown. He knows the club, he knows the players and he knows exactly what's expected of him in the City set-up. He's not Pep, but things aren't about to drop off a cliff.

‌

Sports.title: Rangers chief stuns shareholders by comparing Derek McInnes to Jurgen Klopp
Sports.content:
Rangers chief stuns shareholders by comparing Derek McInnes to Jurgen Klopp

Rangers have endured a winless start to the season under new boss Derek McInnes but their chief executive has compared him to Jurgen Klopp in a shareholders meeting

View 2 Images Derek McInnes is yet to win as Rangers boss

Rangers shareholders were told to see Derek McInnes as "a Jurgen Klopp-type manager" by chief executive Jim Gillespie as he defended the under fire boss.

‌



McInnes was appointed at Ibrox off the back of a stellar spell at Hearts, that saw him come within minutes of winning the Scottish title last year, only to be upset by Celtic in a dramatic final day. They were still able to finish above Rangers, who quickly moved to hire him.

‌



However, Rangers have endured a poor start to the season and Sunday's defeat at home to Hibernian means they are already five points off the pace set by bitter rivals Celtic after only two games.

‌



The Scottish giants have held a meeting of their shareholders and Gillespie's comparison of McInnes and Klopp has raised eyebrows. The German has just taken charge of his national side but is regarded among the greatest managers of the modern era.

When asked by a shareholder to explain what attracted the club to the McInnes Gillespie replied: “You have two types of managers — a Klopp-type manager and a [Pep] Guardiola type. We think Derek is a Klopp type, someone who plays front-foot football and wants to win. Derek is the only manager who ticked all our boxes.”

McInnes didn't attend the meeting, and when pressed on that club chief Andrew Cavenagh explained that the panel had been arranged months ago but McInnes' focus was at the training ground to help prepare the team, who are in Europa League qualifying action on Thursday.

‌



The new Rangers boss has come out fighting following their slow start and maintains that the team are not as bad as the outside noise suggests.

View 2 Images Klopp won the Premier League with Liverpool and is regarded as one of their greatest managers (Image: LAURENCE GRIFFITHS/POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

"We're not as bad as some people will be saying at the minute," he told Sky Sports. "And I think it's important that we just batten down the hatches, stay strong, stay together. We try, as a club, to come out of this window strong and we will.

Article continues below

"At the minute, we're trying to manage the situation. Some players are not quite as fit but we need to get them playing to get them fit. We're not at the start we wanted but we still plan to get the finish and the outcome that we want and we'll work towards that."

Sports.title: Jose Mourinho fires clear dig at old foe Pep Guardiola: 'I hate that word'
Sports.content:
Jose Mourinho fires clear dig at old foe Pep Guardiola: 'I hate that word'

Jose Mourinho hasn't spent a year out of management in more than two decades and has claimed he'll never take a sabbatical, suggesting its a sign of weakness

View 2 Images Jose Mourinho has underlined his desire to continue managing (Image: Netflix)

Jose Mourinho seems to have fired a dig at long-time rival Pep Guardiola as he claimed a "sabbatical means weakness" with the Catalan currently taking some time out.

‌



Guardiola has just ended his 10-year spell with Manchester City and, despite the offer of work in the international scene, he wants to take some time out. He famously took a year out after leaving Barcelona in 2012, before assuming his role at Bayern Munich.

‌



It was his years at Barcelona, where he faced Mourinho's Real Madrid, that prompted Guardiola's first sabbatical. The Catalan is ultimately renowned for his intensity and taking him away is only natural.

‌



However, the Special One has highlighted how he's never needed to spend time out of the game. His spells out of management have simply come whilst he's been waiting for a job to come up and Mourinho maintains sabbaticals aren't for him.

Jose Mourinho reveals he signed contract to succeed Sir Alex Ferguson at Man Utd READ MORE :

He said in his Netflix Documentary: “Some guys, they need a sabbatical – which is something that I hate. I hate that word. For me, sabbatical means weakness. Don’t speak with me about sabbaticals. I never need a rest. I will have a rest when he (Mourinho points to the sky) decides to say: ‘Come up’.”

Since shooting to prominence with Porto in the early 2000s, the longest stint Mourinho has had out of management was 11 months - that coming between his Manchester United sacking in December 2018 and him taking on the Tottenham job in November 2019.

‌



Mourinho, now 63, has returned to Real this summer for a second spell and signed a three-year contract. The Portuguese boss admits he cannot foresee a day when he's not in management.

View 2 Images In contrast to Pep Guardiola, Jose Mourinho insists he wouldn't take a sabbatical (Image: PA)

He said: “I cannot even imagine when I am going to stop my life in football. I say 10 more years, but maybe more than 10. It’s fun. It was, it is and will always be fun. I want to win more titles. I want to win new titles. I want to repeat titles.

‌



“I want to do it in places where I have never been. I want to do it in places where I did before. My world is to walk in a football stadium with 50,000 or 90,000 [fans]. I had 100,000. That is my world.

“Without football, there is not something complete in me. But I don’t think it is an obsession. I don’t feel it as an obsession. It is just when you reach a certain level, you want to stay there forever.”

Sports.title: What's happening with Marcus Rashford? Man Utd return, transfer stance, telling gesture
Sports.content:
What's happening with Marcus Rashford? Man Utd return, transfer stance, telling gesture

Marcus Rashford's future remains the topic of plenty of speculation as he returns to Manchester United after spending last season out on loan

View 3 Images Marcus Rashford has rejoined his Manchester United team-mates after a spell out on loan (Image: Richard Sellers/Sportsphoto/Allstar via Getty Images)

A few months ago, the idea of Marcus Rashford returning to the fold at Manchester United looked far-fetched. Strange things can happen in football, though, and the England international's Old Trafford comeback is right up there

‌



Rashford spent last season on loan at Barcelona and looked poised for a permanent move to Spotify Camp Nou. However, the Catalan club let their £26m option expire.

‌



For as long as Ruben Amorim was in the United dugout, a return for the forward looked impossible. However, the arrival of Michael Carrick - a former team-mate of Rashford - has altered the picture.

‌



England's run to the World Cup semi-finals meant a later return for the 28-year-old than for some of his colleagues. Now, though, Rashford's future is very much at the forefront of discussions.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Man Utd given Benjamin Sesko reality check after Bayern Munich transfer links READ MORE :

Man Utd return

Following United's 1-1 draw with PSG on Saturday, Carrick confirmed that Rashford has returned as part of his first team group, alongside Kobbie Mainoo.

‌



“We have got a full squad this week in Dublin. We fly straight there and have a few days where we have the whole group back together," United's manager said. “Marcus is part of that, and Kobbie and Lisandro [Martinez]. We look forward to seeing them.”

View 3 Images Rashford has joined the United camp in Dublin (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Get Man United's new 2026/27 home kit This article contains affiliate links, we will receive a commission on any sales we generate from it. Learn more £85 Fanatics Buy Now on Fanatics Product Description Manchester United have launched their new home kit for the 2026/27 season, i nspired by the club's heritage and featuring a classic polo collar with iconic adidas details.

‌



As reported by the MEN, the England pair joined Benjamin Sesko, Senne Lammens, Matheus Cunha, Matthijs de Ligt, Karl Darlow, JJ Gabriel and Tynan Thompson on a private jet to Dublin. Some of those players could play a part in United's midweek friendly with Leeds, with Martinez also expected in Dublin.

Transfer stance

Rashford is not interested in moving to Turkey or Saudi Arabia, thereby limiting his options. He would only join a European side who can offer him Champions League football. There are only so many clubs capable of meeting the forward's demands and one of them, Barcelona, are already out of the running barring a big U-turn.

The fee might not be a huge obstacle, with the MEN suggesting £25m - a little less than the provisional sum agreed with Barca - potentially enough to do it. However, those close to Rashford are said to have suggested United are no longer desperate to sell.

‌



Rashford will be with the rest of the squad for United's final two pre-season friendlies, against Leeds on Wednesday and AC Milan on Saturday, and is expected to be around for the Premier League opener away at Hull on August 22.

View 3 Images Barcelona allowed their £26m transfer option to expire (Image: Aitor Alcalde Colomer/Getty Images)

Telling gesture

While some fans are prepared to wait and see when it comes to Rashford's future, others have been looking for clues wherever they can find them. One such clue comes on the squad number front, where the forward is set to wear No. 14 next term.

Article continues below

United have already given Matheus Cunha the No. 10 previously worn by the England international and there are no indications it will revert back to its previous owner. Rashford wore No. 14 at Barcelona, though, and the choice can be read as an indication that the club and Carrick consider him part of their plans.

The No. 14 shirt was vacant for United last season. The number was not reused when Christian Eriksen left the club, while previous holders include Jesse Lingard and Javier Hernandez.

Sports.title: Rising star Oleksandr Khyzhniak to fight for first boxing title
Sports.content:
Rising star Oleksandr Khyzhniak to fight for first boxing title

Khyzhniak made his debut earlier this year and made his second appearance on the undercard of Anthony Joshua's win over Kristrian Prenga last month

View Image Oleksandr Khyzhniak is a rising star

Oleksandr Khyzhniak, who many believe can follow in mentor Oleksandr Usyk's footsteps, will fight for his first title later this month.

‌



Khyzhniak made his debut earlier this year and made his second appearance on the undercard of Anthony Joshua's win over Kristrian Prenga last month. He will now headline the second boxing event put on by Usyk's promotional company Usyk 17 Promotions on August 22.

‌



The event, to be held at !FESTrepublic in Lviv, will be dedicated to the 35th anniversary of Ukraine's independence and Usyk said: “Thirty-five years of independent development is actually not a very long time. Twelve of those years have been lived under conditions of war. But look at how much we have already managed to achieve despite everything.

‌



Anthony Joshua sets out demands to move Tyson Fury fight to New York READ MORE :

"Look at the incredible athletes we have — not only boxers, but Olympic champions and Paralympians. Artists, musicians, scientists. We want to remember our greatest victories, honour those who fought and continue to fight for our freedom, and show the entire world that Ukraine has been, is and will remain a country of strong, talented and unbreakable people.”

Sergey Lapin, who is guiding Khyzhniak in his professional career, added:“A first title fight is both a natural and an important step in Oleksandr’s professional career. He is ready for a new level of competition and to prove his quality in championship fights. For Usyk 17 Promotions, it is especially important that this stage of his journey begins in Ukraine — at our second boxing event in Lviv. Our goal is to build a platform in Ukraine where the strongest boxers can develop, win titles and confidently progress to the international level.”

Article continues below

The fight night's co-main event will feature Pavlo Illiusha while the undercard will include nine Usyk 17 Promotions boxers in Maksym Rudyk, Maksym Zymenko, Dmytro Lovchynskyi, Elvin Aliiev, Bohdan Tolmachov, Mykola Laktionov, Jamal Kuliev, Aider Abduraimov and Matvii Razhba.

Sports.title: Inside Jeff Bezos' stunning £208bn empire and mansions as he prepares for Liverpool investment
Sports.content:
Inside Jeff Bezos' stunning £208bn empire and mansions as he prepares for Liverpool investment

Billionaire Amazon founder Jeff Bezos is involved in a consortium looking to buy into Liverpool with a statement anticipated soon

View 3 Images Jeff Bezos is part of a consortium looking to take a stake in Liverpool (Image: Kevin Mazur/Getty Images for The Met Museum/Vogue)

Jeff Bezos is preparing to take a stake in Liverpool. The billionaire is part of a consortium which also includes Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin.

‌



Amazon founder Bezos has been one of the richest men in the world for a number of years. He sat fourth on the most recent Forbes billionaires list, with his fortune now estimated to sit at $280bn (just under £208m).

‌



According to Sky News, an official announcement over the deal could arrive this week. The consortium is reportedly led by Amit Bhatia, the former QPR chairman and son-in-law of Indian billionaire Lakshmi Mittal.

‌



An investment in Liverpool would just be the latest step for the super-rich businessman, who boasts a huge property empire along with wife Lauren Sanchez. Here, we've taken a deeper dive into what that looks like.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Reports from Realtor.com estimates Bezos' property empire to be worth some $500m (£370m) on its own. The star of the show is his primary home on Indian Creek Island in Florida, an exclusive island with just 34 residences - unsurprisingly belonging to the super-rich.

Three of those belong to Bezos, including a $90m property bought in 2024. While the size of the home means he might not have neighbours in the same sense as you or I, other residents of Indian Creek Island include NFL legend Tom Brady and first daughter Ivanka Trump.

Previously, Bezos lived in Seattle with his former wife Mackenzie Scott and still owns a number of properties in the area. He made a tidy profit on one of his homes in the small town of Hunts Point, buying for $37.5m in 2019 and selling for $63m four years later, per the Puget Sound Business Journal.

‌



View 3 Images Bezos owns property on the exclusive Indian Creek Island (Image: Google Maps)

Get Liverpool's new 2026/27 home kit This article contains affiliate links, we will receive a commission on any sales we generate from it. Learn more £85 LFC Shop Buy Now on LFC Shop Product Description Liverpool FC have launched their new home kit for the 2026/27, inspired by iconic adidas strip worn during the club's 1989/90 title-winning campaign.

The 62-year-old established Amazon in Washington State in the 90s and also purchased properties in the Seattle suburb of Medina. He isn't the only Hunts Point resident with ties to Seattle, with former Seattle Seahawks NFL coach Pete Carroll among the others to buy property there.

‌



Over the last decade, Bezos has also picked up properties in Washington DC and New York City, each worth more than $15m, and a ranch in West Texas. That's nothing compared to his $78m Hawaii property, though, which is believed to include a 4,500-square-foot main house.

However, it's a $165m Beverly Hills home which tops the lot. The California property was developed by movie mogul Jack Warner and previously belonged to record executive David Geffen, with Architectural Digest reporting that it includes tennis courts and its own nine-hole golf course.

View 3 Images Bezos and wife Lauren Sanchez also own properties in Texas and California worth millions of dollars (Image: Google Maps)

‌



It isn't just about property for Bezos either. The bulk of his wealth still comes from his Amazon stake, despite him selling shares worth a reported $13.5bn in 2023, while he has a private investment firm - Bezos Expeditions - which manages his other investments.

These investments include stakes in Uber and Airbnb, among other ventures, with the Sovereign Wealth Fund Institute estimating Bezos investments has approximately $107.8bn of assets. The billionaire also took charge of the Washington Post more than a decade ago in a deal worth $250m.

Another significant project of Bezos is Blue Origin, the space technology company he established in 2000. The company, which produces rockets and engines, was described in 2023 by CEO Bob Smith as having "hundreds of millions in revenue as well as billions of dollars in orders".

Article continues below

While Bezos is one of the richest individuals in the world, fellow consortium member Saverin is reportedly worth nearly $24bn himself. The 44-year-old is a co-founder of venture capital firm B Capital and is now based in Singapore.

Sky News reports that the bid values Liverpool at around $6bn. The club was valued at $4.5bn when Dynasty Equity took a small stake in 2023, though the Bezos-Saverin consortium could take a stake of more than 30 per cent.

Sports.title: Liverpool set to announce new signing but team-mate 'already wants him back' after goodbyes
Sports.content:
Liverpool set to announce new signing but team-mate 'already wants him back' after goodbyes

Ronald Araujo is poised to join Liverpool on a season-long loan from Barcelona, but one team-mate is gutted to be losing his pal this month, and hopes to see him return next year

View 2 Images Ronald Araujo is set to sign for Liverpool on a season-long loan. (Image: NurPhoto, NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Ronald Araujo is already wanted back at Barcelona, despite his transfer to Liverpool not yet being officially confirmed. The defender is set to sign a season-long loan with the Reds.

‌



The arrival of the Uruguay international will ease some of the defensive worries that Andoni Iraola may have as the club builds up to the Premier League season opener against Newcastle United in under two weeks' time. The 27-year-old can play as a central defender or right-back.

‌



Liverpool will have a £47 million option to make the transfer permanent next summer if the loan spell goes well. But, Araujo's Barcelona team-mate Fermin Lopez is hoping that's not the case.

‌



Jeff Bezos to become Liverpool co-owner as FSG agree to sell HUGE stake in club READ MORE :

Liverpool news: Andoni Iraola transfer position emerges as Reds handed Bradley Barcola update READ MORE :

Speaking to Spanish publication Sport, he said: "He (Araujo) has come to say goodbye.

"It's a shame, because he's a captain and I have a good relationship with him. He made the decision to continue developing and I hope he comes back next season."

Araujo has spent the past eight years at Barcelona and has worn the captain's armband at the Nou Camp since being appointed to the role in January.

‌



View 2 Images Fermin Lopez is sad to see his Barcelona team-mate go (Image: Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

Yet he struggled to nail down a regular starting berth, managing just 16 starts last season — a campaign during which he stepped away from the game for mental health reasons. Barcelona manager Hansi Flick has shed light on his decision to allow the defender to depart this summer.

"I think Ronald is a great guy and a fantastic player," he said.

‌



"I think our style of play, that we want to play, is a little bit different. He's a player that has a lot of speed, he's physical and very strong and also with the ball he's quite good.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

"We couldn't include him like I wanted and also I think he wants to make something new. You know it more than me because in the past, something has happened, so this affected him.

Article continues below

"I saw him this morning and I said goodbye and I think he was very happy and Liverpool is also a fantastic club. I wish him all the best because he deserves it.

"He's a fantastic guy and fantastic player and was a great captain."

Sports.title: Harry Kane to respond to Barcelona transfer interest with new bumper contract
Sports.content:
Harry Kane to respond to Barcelona transfer interest with new bumper contract

The England captain has entered the final year of his contract with Bayern Munich.

View 2 Images Harry Kane looks set to extend his stay at Bayern Munich. (Image: Adam Pretty/Getty Images)

England captain Harry Kane will reportedly extend his Bayern Munich contract by a further two years, as the German side ward off interest from Barcelona. The striker has entered the final year of his current deal at the Allianz Arena.

Reports suggested that Barcelona were interested in signing Kane this summer as the search for a replacement for Robert Lewandowski. However, it seems that a stay in Germany is on the cards.

The Times reports that the 33-year-old is set to extend his contract until 2029, with no significant change to his current salary. Kane is one of the top earners at Bayern Munich, with a yearly wage of around £21.5million per year.

‌



Aston Villa linked with bargain Real Madrid transfer to replace Morgan Rogers READ MORE :

Everton and Crystal Palace agree stunning swap deal as Lamine Camara bid rejected READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

The striker is yet to return to pre-season, having had an extended break following this summer’s World Cup with England. He captained the Three Lions to a third-place finish in the tournament.

He is expected to meet up with his teammates later this week as the club prepares for their Bundesliga opener against Stuttgart on Friday, 28 August (7.30pm BST).

Before that, they play Borussia Dortmund in the German Super Cup final on Saturday, 22 August (7.30pm BST).

Kane scored 61 goals in 51 games in all competitions for Bayern last season, helping them to lift the Bundesliga crown for the second season in a row. He will look to continue that impressive goalscoring record in the new campaign.

View 2 Images Harry Kane captained England in this summer's World Cup. (Image: Eddie Keogh - The FA/The FA via Getty Images)

‌



The report adds that there is an 'expectation' that Kane will eventually return to the Premier League as he bids to break Alan Shearer’s long-standing goalscoring record. He currently has 213 goals in the league, 47 away from Shearer’s record of 260.

There has been consistent talk of a possible return to Tottenham Hotspur, where he scored all of his Premier League goals after coming through the academy, but it seems that Spurs will have to wait a bit longer for a possible reunion.

Kane left the club in 2023, with Spurs receiving a fee of around £86million from Bayern Munich.

In his time in Germany so far, he has scored 146 goals in 147 appearances for the club.
