World.title: ‎Police rescue 15 kidnap victims after gun battle in Kogi
World.content:
By Boluwaji Obahopo, Lokoja

‎

‎The Kogi State Police Command has rescued 15 victims abducted along the Itobe–Anyigba highway in Ofu Local Government Area of the state after a fierce gun battle with their abductors.

‎

‎The victims, including two personnel of the Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) and three children, were rescued from the kidnappers’ custody following a coordinated security operation on Sunday.

‎

‎The incident occurred at about 4pm on Sunday, August 9, 2026, when a Peace Mass Transit bus was intercepted between Ojuwo Ajengo and Mamerebo, an identified kidnapping flashpoint along the Itobe–Achigili axis of the highway.

‎

‎The abductors reportedly took the occupants of the bus into the surrounding forest before security operatives mobilised to the area.

‎

‎Following the incident, the Commissioner of Police, Kogi State Command, CP Naziru Bello Kankarofi, ordered the immediate deployment of tactical and intelligence assets to track the kidnappers and rescue the victims.

‎

‎The operation involved personnel of the Police, 12 Brigade of the Nigerian Army, Department of State Services (DSS), Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), local vigilantes and other auxiliary security forces.

‎

‎According to a statement by the Police Public Relations Officer, ASP Saliu Oyiza Afusat, the operatives engaged the abductors in a fierce gun battle during the rescue operation.

‎

‎”Several of the kidnappers were neutralised during the encounter, while others fled into the surrounding forest.

‎

‎”However, a local vigilante member supporting the security operation was killed, while a police officer sustained gunshot injuries.

‎

‎”Despite the resistance, the security operatives closed in on the abductors and successfully rescued all 15 victims directly from their custody.

‎

‎”The rescued victims comprise 12 adults and three children, including two FRSC personnel. They were found safe and unharmed and were evacuated from the operational area to safety.

‎

‎”The rescued victims are: CRC I. Ibe and SRC Ik. Ukandu, both FRSC personnel; Josephbah; Joshua Daniel; Joy Ogbu; Chigocife Ogbu; Charity Aneebo; Ngozi Stephin; Somaliya Zegu; Chidera Emanuel; Pamela Oraeto; Abakwam Loveth; Chimereze Nekuma; Chibok Nzekwu; and Victor Edozi Anyichie.”

‎

‎The command said efforts were ongoing to apprehend the fleeing abductors, while tactical and intelligence-driven operations were being sustained in the area.

‎

‎It added that three other coordinated security operations were also ongoing at different locations across the state as part of efforts to disrupt criminal activities and protect residents.

‎

‎The police urged members of the public to remain vigilant and provide timely and credible information that could assist security agencies in apprehending criminal elements.

‎

‎The command assured residents of its commitment to protecting lives and property and sustaining operations aimed at dismantling criminal networks across the state

World.title: Alleged IVF Fraud: AGF takes over trial of Abuja Doctor, 2 others
World.content:
Attorney General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Prince Lateef Fagbemi

By Ikechukwu Nnochiri

ABUJA— The Attorney General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Prince Lateef Fagbemi, SAN, has taken over the prosecution of Abuja-based fertility doctor, John Abebe, accused of fraud and unlawful disclosure of confidential medical records of a patient.

Also cited as 2nd and 3rd defendants in the three-count charge marked CR/005/2026 are Joje Abebe Facility Centre Limited and Balikis Bakare.

According to the FG, the defendants unlawfully revealed the confidential medical records of a patient, Mrs. Mary Manga, without consent, thereby violating her right to medical confidentiality contrary to the provisions of the National Health Act, 2014.

The prosecution further alleged that the 1st defendant breached a confidentiality agreement relating to the reproductive health status of Mrs. Manga’s husband by attaching confidential medical records to a pre-action demand notice issued through his lawyers.

It told the court that the said documents became accessible to third parties, causing emotional trauma to the complainants.

In count three of the charge, it was alleged that the embattled medical doctor had, between January and May 2025, fraudulently obtained N19 million from the complainants by falsely representing himself as an in vitro fertilization (IVF) specialist.

According to the FG, the 1st defendant converted both the money and the embryos extracted from the patients to his personal use, contrary to the Advance Fee Fraud and Other Related Offences Act, 2006.

Though it was the Nigeria Police Force (NPF) that initially filed the charge before a High Court of the Federal Capital Territory, Abuja, the AGF applied to take over the prosecution.

The defendants had since pleaded their innocence to the allegations, even as trial Justice A. A. Fashola, in a ruling on March 11, released them on bail pending the determination of the case.

World.title: Coup allegation: I acted out of patriotism, frustration with Nigeria — Army Colonel Ma’aji
World.content:
ABUJA — A Nigerian Army Colonel, Mohammed Ma’aji, accused of involvement in an alleged plot to overthrow the government of President Bola Tinubu, has said his actions were driven by patriotism and frustration over what he described as worsening conditions in the country.

Ma’aji, in a statement made available on Monday, apologised for his involvement in the alleged plot and appealed to the authorities for leniency, insisting that his motive was not personal ambition but a desire for a better Nigeria.

He said the alleged plan emerged from concerns among some military personnel over poor governance, insecurity, inadequate welfare and declining living standards.

According to him, the situation had become so troubling that he feared the country was heading towards collapse.

Ma’aji said: “What has happened has a very long history, and it is driven by patriotism and I love the job and country.

“Every time I look at how I’m struggling to raise five children with my meagre salary, I get worried. Looking at every aspect of life in Nigeria, there is no hope for the common man, and we are left to defend ourselves.

“This has nothing to do with any ambition or personal goals. It is purely out of the desire for a prosperous country that works for everyone.”

He alleged that military personnel were particularly affected by inadequate welfare, citing the condition of soldiers wounded in combat and the challenges facing serving personnel and their families.

The colonel said the alleged movement was still at a stage of mobilisation and discussions when security authorities intervened, adding that no specific date had been agreed for any action.

He also denied that there were foreign collaborators, while explaining that various individuals became involved at different stages of the discussions.

Ma’aji said some of those approached expressed concerns about the state of the country, while others withdrew or failed to provide the resources they had initially promised.

He further said the alleged plot was fuelled by what he described as frustrations over his failure to secure promotion to the rank of brigadier-general on two occasions.

According to him, some of his colleagues had encouraged him to revive the movement after the second setback.

The colonel, however, said his experience following his arrest had changed his perspective and made him realise that there were alternative ways of expressing concerns within the military.

“If God willing, the authority is kind enough to pardon us, we will never contemplate this course of action again in the future,” he said.

Ma’aji called for the establishment of a formal channel through which military personnel could communicate their concerns directly to the Chief of Army Staff without fear of victimisation.

He also recommended improved remuneration and welfare packages for members of the Armed Forces, including better healthcare, housing, pension and family support.

He called for an improvement in the military’s casualty management system, saying the treatment of wounded soldiers could affect the morale of personnel still serving in operational areas.

He also criticised what he described as godfatherism and perceived inequality in military postings and career progression, arguing that some officers had spent years on operations while others had little or no operational exposure.

On the wider Nigerian society, Ma’aji expressed concern over the cost of living, education, corruption and the impact of fuel subsidy removal on ordinary citizens.

He urged the government to invest resources saved from subsidy reforms in programmes capable of reducing hardship, including mass transportation and other social infrastructure.

He also called for stronger action against corruption, saying perceived impunity among public officials could affect the morale and confidence of security personnel.

On the alleged coup plot itself, Ma’aji said the movement was never intended to destabilise the country, insisting that it was motivated by what he described as love for Nigeria.

He said: “Everything we planned was born out of patriotism, love of country, and the desire to have a prosperous Nigeria that we all can be proud of.”

The colonel appealed to the authorities to consider the circumstances that led to the alleged plot and pardon those involved, describing them as first offenders.

“We are pleading for a pardon and a chance to amend our ways. Many of the officers have participated in some operations in the North-East. I am happy nobody has been hurt,” he said.

Ma’aji said his detention had been “challenging and revealing”, adding that it had given him an opportunity to reconsider his approach to expressing grievances.

He maintained that he and others involved had no other country to call their own and urged the authorities to consider their contributions to national security alongside the allegations against them.

He concluded by asking for an opportunity to meet with the relevant authorities, apologise and commit themselves to pursuing lawful and peaceful means of addressing grievances.

Read his full statement as obtained by Premium Times

COLONEL MA’AJI’S VERBATIM STATEMENT IN FULL

First and foremost, I want to clearly apologise for what has happened. You will call that we are all human and are bound to make mistakes.

What has happened has a very long history, and it is driven by patriotism and I love the job and country. As we are all sitting down here, we have our biases and our thoughts and concerns on what was going on in our country from a state of gradual decline up to now, and we are almost at the point of collapse. I’m sure even one of you must have had the cause to reflect on the situation of the nation.

Every time I look at how I’m struggling to raise 5 children with my meager salary, I get worried. I attended Army Day Secondary School, but today, how many of us afford to take our children to these schools, and for one reason or the other, which is connected to the bad governance. Looking at every aspect of life in Nigeria, there is no hope for the common man, and we are left to defend ourselves. This has nothing to do with any ambition or personal goals. It is purely out of the desire for a prosperous country that works for everyone.

Most of these leaders have different nationalities and are citizens of other countries, and don’t have anything to lose, unlike us, that Nigeria is our only country. Take a drive to Kaduna, go to 44 Nigeria Army Reference Hospital and see the plight of our soldiers, sir. What you will see will shock you. Soldiers and officers who sustained injury in combat have been abandoned to their fate.

The summary of all this is that this action was driven by the desire to have a prosperous nation and country that we all can be proud of. It got to a point that I was worried that if nothing is done, we may not have a country to call our own in the near future. Nigeria was turning into a banana republic right before our eyes. We know that during the era of the military regime, the country was functioning better. I believe that, as it is now, we are on a dangerous trajectory.

I know that this general conspiracy of silence and sentiment is holding all of us, but we can move above it. We were waiting to.grow in rank from Lt to Gen, yet we could not see the change we wanted. We needed to tell the civilians when they are wrong and register that we have done our best. I did not mean bad for anybody, either a superior, subordinate, or peers alike. It was a genuine act to contribute my own quota and stop going to bed grumbling without action. It baffles me that a country like Nigeria, blessed with enough mineral and human resources, could be ridiculously regarded as the poverty capital of the world.

This started years ago till we got to this point of no return, where we are now. Anybody who genuinely loves this country and interacts with officers and soldiers will agree that most of us share this concern.

When I see a person who has a genuine concern about the precarious situation of our country, I throw up the discussion. I am mostly drawn to officers who genuinely reason in the same line that was how the movement started. The plan was to get enough officers of like minds who could participate. We were still at the stage of mobilizing to get more officers involved. Since at my level I am not a BDE commander or a GOC so we needed officers who could bring in resources.

There are officers that I did not talk to directly, but if any officer I am close to recommends them, I give them the go-ahead to talk with the officers. Sqn Ldr Zuzu was introduced through DB Abdullahi and Sqn Ldr SB Adamu, whom I got to know about him and he attended one of our meetings at Brookville, and he said he was going to get back on the roles he could play to assist the movement.

In this movement, a substantial amount spent are my personal resources. Timiprey Silva only came in recently. His own contribution was coming in bulk; mine, don’t have the records of how much I had spent. I think Timprey Silver has contributed about 400 million naira, and there are no foreign collaborations.

The only senior officer that I can say was aware was Brig Gen Sadiq, but he withdrew mainly based on the issue of resources and the need to get more senior officers involved, and since that time, whenever we discuss, it’s just about the challenge and how to involve more senior officers. However, after that, we did not go beyond that.

I never spoke to Gen Jalo or Gen Danja about the plan. I have also never spoken to Navy Capt Victor, rtd, about the movement. Another person, however, who was deeply involved was Col MM Adamu rtd. He also said that some senior officers close to him were also concerned about the country, which he intended to engage them at his own level.

I got to recruit Zekeri Umor through Insp Ahmed Ibrahim, who works in the villa too. Ahmed, on the other hand, I got close to him when we visited my wife’s restaurant, and also through Cpl Audu, who was close to me and had served in the villa before, we did not start based on the plot. The restaurant is called Kakaki restaurant on Mahatma Gandhi Street. The restaurant was closed when the owner sold the property.

Mostly when officers come for a meeting, you give them transport because they really don’t have. The situation is so bad that some officers cannot even afford to buy cars or even transport themselves from point A to B.

At first, Zekeri requested N1 billion to assist in getting access to the Villa, and I told him that we are stirred by patriotism, not money, and whatever was available, I would share with him.

The recruitment of CJTF was Iliyasu’s idea. When I went to the North East for a wedding, Maj Iliyasu met me and asked how far about the movement was and complained that there was no manpower. He then said he had CJTF working for 7 Div, then that we could use them. I asked him how; he said they were good, and that he could mobilize them. I asked him about weapons and he told me they already had their personal rifles. Then I asked how he was going to move them to Abuja, and these movement plans were not finalized.

This team has not been fully formed because there were supposed to be other meetings. There was no D-Day. We were waiting for the availability of resources and more officers and soldiers. I know that Hayatu and Dangnap are supposed to generate troops, but no date has been specifically given to them.

But they both said they had enough ammo, weapons, vehicles, and troops.

The essence of asking them to send pictures and the given task was to place the service chiefs under arrest in the house, and not to cause interference with the movement. The coup was supposed to be carried out at night.

Bappah has his own plans for 102 Bn because he said he stays in the unit, and he said they have some equipment that could be used.

The key persons to be arrested are as written in the paper seen at my house Col Adamu (rt) is a key player, actually, and he was supposed to also source for funds, but he has not been able to cope with his promise to make contact with some senior officers.

WO Nasir has attended the meeting twice; his boys were more or less like a standby force. I have known WO Nasiru for a very long time, from NDA when I was a cadet.

If you interact with officers and soldiers, 80 percent are disgruntled already. And it was a voluntary thing nobody was coerced. In these recent efforts, I had given up the motive, but some of these officers kept texting and calling for my intervention. There were none who after I spoke to them, drew back after sharing the plan with them. The desire for the change is genuine, and that has been what has kept the plan alive for a long time.

I and Col M Adamu had always been friends even while he was in the service. I did not talk to Lt Col AI Almakura of Artillery about this plan.

You see the genuine efforts that the Nigerian youths have tried to get back their country, you saw the End SARS protest, you saw the recent Get Back Our Country protests, End Bad Government protest too.

If the avenue for dialogue or protest or all non-violent avenues were available, they would have been utilized to prevent the country from deteriorating further as a result of the endemic corruption. All these protests were avenues for the peaceful resolution of national issues but all were rushed and opportunity lost. This is not about us alone, but the country in general.

When I was denied my first attempt for Brig Gen. Nobody up till today called me to tell me why, so also the second attempt. If our leaders are caring, that should not have been the case. In fact, after I lost my second attempt, many of the boys called me and said oga, we told you there is no other option than to go ahead with our plans and that was how the movement was revived again.

I have met Maj D Yusuf, and I don’t know his level of involvement. I also do not know Capt Benuga. Maj A Mohammed is also not involved. Brig Gen Sadiq was aware when he was a Garrison Commander in Lagos. Lt Col B Almustapha is also not a part. Maj A ldris has not been regular in meetings, but he is aware of the plans. Lt Col AImakura was in the know of the plans, and I discussed it with him around 2023; however, since he assumed command in Abuja, I have not contacted him.

Maj Usman was to get resources from 45 Bn, Lt Col Dangnap was to bring sources from 134 Bn, Maj AJ Ibrahim was to get resources from 198. Aminu John was not part of the plan. Whenever I am looking for cash, I just reach out to him to get the cash or mint. FM Ali is also not involved.

To prevent the reoccurrence of such incidents like this I would advise the authority as follows

Poor Remuneration: The salary of Nigerian Armed Forces personnel is too low, considering the current economic realities and inflation.

Welfare: For instance, we are an army at war; our handling of casualties is paramount to how the rest working will be willing to continue and lay their lives for the country. There is also a need for robust welfare packages for all the members of the Armed Forces. There is also a need for serving personnel’s family welfare packages to be introduced. The COAS Loan Program should be expanded and sustained.

The AF NHIS package needs to be reviewed to include more critical health challenges rather than just malaria and typhoid. There is a need for a sustainable housing program for the Armed Forces rather than isolated and disjointed packages. The issue of the Obasanjo car loan scheme needs to come back. I think the AFN needs a whole department dedicated to personnel welfare. I could elaborate on this if given the opportunity.

Godfatherism: A system where you can hardly get anything without someone calling in on your behalf. There are officers who have been 8, 9 years straight on operations. While we still have some officers who haven’t been to the North East and will never be there.

Pension Upgrade: Col Adamu told me that his pension cannot buy his BP drugs. I feel sad when I saw CDS ordering ex-servicemen to be dispersed from their protest ground for improved pensions. We should remember that we shall all retire. Our ex-servicemen deserve better treatment. Charity begins at home; that is why I am starting from the armed forces.

Removal of fuel subsidy: The government should have phased the removal and not the sudden removal, and the policy is anti-human. The primary purpose of government, as provided by the Constitution, is the welfare and security of the people… we have rather created more stealing avenues because governors now have more funds to steal. An average Nigerian is not asking for too much, just a bare minimum of being able to move from point A to B and also afford 3 square meals, good health, and the education of their children. The federal Government should invest the subsidy money in a practical project that can reduce human suffering. The issue of Urban Mass Transit that started during the military regime should be revisited.

Corruption: This must be given clear and serious attention because it is the mother of all crimes. The examples of Yaya Bello, Emiefele, the former accountant general, all these people are yet to face justice, and then these soldiers are watching these, and you do not expect vulnerability or reaction?

Education: Our education is in shambles. Those of us here in Abuja, how much do we pay for school fees, and how many officers/soldiers can afford school fees with their salaries?

Budget padding: After padding a budget and awarding costs, they’re still not implemented. For example, you put 1 thousand naira for a water of 100 naira and still do not buy the water.

These are people who got almost everything free, including education when growing up, but there is no free education anywhere today in Nigeria. They all turned their backs against the country. As a service personnel, how much of salary can you save that would buy you a house to live in ? Is it after using all your youthful years that you will start looking for money to survive after retirement?

Some officers have served for over 15 years, and even a plot of land they don’t have. The policy of car loans was swept under the carpet. What happened to all these policies? An average officer or soldier is barely surviving. Despite the huge sacrifices they are making on a daily basis to keep the country safe and secured.

There is no well-spelt out channel of communication to the COAS if an officer wishes to have any interaction with him. There is a need to institutionalize a channel of communication for officers to air their concerns without being witch-haunted.

Timiprey Silva is someone that I have known since as a Capt but I never discussed this issue with him until just recently and it was still pushed from all these boys. When I did, he said Col please I don’t want to hear about this but later he then called and asked to know more of the details and asked about the chances of success. He said he’s a politician, but he does not think current politicians have the audacity to return the country to track. He said he sent all his children abroad because of the unfavourable conditions of Nigeria as a country.

There were considerations of 27 September, 1 Oct, and a month after as the possible D-Day, but it was not concluded as no specific day was agreed. Sqn Ldr Zuzu introduced by Lt Cdre Abdullahi, that he had conversed with the officer and that the officer is seriously disgruntled, and I gave him the go-ahead to invite him for a meeting. I sent him money as welfare and not to buy me golf kits as I don’t play golf. I asked about the whereabouts of his family in order to be sure they were out of Abuja.

WO Nasiru said he has some contacts of influencers, but I don’t know them.

Col Adamu was supposed to procure radios from a link he had in Kaduna, but has not been given the money to procure them yet.

From the time I have been arrested till now, If I were to be released and these issues in the country persist, I will consider a different approach. The past 2 or 3 weeks I have been arrested has been quite challenging and revealing, and it has served as an eye opener for me. I have come to realise that there could be alternative ways of conveying some of these concerns, especially after my interaction with this panel. If God willing, the authority is kind enough to pardon us…,we will never contemplate this course of action again in the future. recommendation for an open channel of communication to the COAS would provide ample opportunity and avenue for officers to register their concerns.

If there was any discussion of IED, it was Maj Iliyasu who said he had some Boko Haram technicians working in the theater to make IED, but I told him that it was not necessary.

My loss of promotion for the second time also contributed to the revival of …the movement to commence again. This is because the boys were … that the injustice would never stop, and as such they are for a revival of the struggle.

There is no evidence that the loss of my first promotion could be attributed to the allegation of my involvement in attempting to disrupt the 2023 election and take the government. All I know is that I was still at AHQ Gar when I was invited for an interview at DIA. I met AVM Owai, who quizzed me on what was going through my mind and I told him nothing. He then said there were allegations that politicians were trying to use me for election. I said that was not the case. And truly, as at that time the movement had died down. Then he requested my phone…. I was detained and advised, and released with a verbal apology.

My application for Schengen VSIA has been long and has nothing to do with the movement. Only one of my daughters got admission to study medicine at Cairo University, Egypt.

I have a passionate appeal to the authorities. It is often said that two wrongs do not make a right. Therefore, on behalf of everyone involved, I want to beg authority to look at the cause and the fundamental issues that drove us into this and address them. We are pleading for leniency and pardon as first offenders. The system should take a deep breath and pardon us. They should give us a chance to mend our ways. We have no other country than Nigeria and no other job. They should also look at some of our sacrifices and not judge us by one mistake. We are pleading for a pardon and a chance to amend our ways. Many of the officers have participated in some operations in the North East. I am happy nobody has been hurt. No action has been taken, and no bullet has been released. Please accept our prayers for leniency and pardon us.

This incident has really opened our eyes and has changed our mindset forever. It was not intended to destabilize the country at all.

Everything we planned was born out of patriotism, love of country, and the desire to have a prosperous Nigeria that we all can be proud of.

We shall also be glad if we should be given the opportunity to interact with ASA face to face and plead forgiveness, and sign an agreement to the effect that we shall never return to the past again in the future. Thank you very much sir.

World.title: Trump says will demand conflict compensation from Iran
World.content:
US President Donald Trump said Monday he would seek conflict compensation from Iran as part of any peace negotiations, citing attacks and atrocities stretching back decades allegedly backed or perpetrated by Tehran.

Iran is “asking for compensation for the damage done to them during the last five month Military Conflict… I am likewise demanding compensation from Iran, for all of the people that they have killed and gravely wounded with their roadside bombs and many conflicts,” Trump posted.

In what has become a regular pattern, Trump last week threatened to hit Iran “very hard”, potentially with attacks against civilian infrastructure, only to pull back, hinting a peace deal was near.

His latest comments on Truth Social came a day after Trump said he was “low-keying” his approach to the conflict, suggesting that he was prepared to let economic pressure mount in place of further military strikes.

Digital media outlet Axios said that the US president did not express any frustration with Iran’s delaying an agreement to open the Strait of Hormuz in their interview with him published Sunday.

Tehran has demanded that the US first end its blockade of Iranian ports and lift sanctions on its oil industry.

As negotiations have stalled, the strait’s blockage by Iran has sent fuel prices soaring and rattled the world economy, putting pressure on Trump ahead of midterm elections in November.

In his post, Trump referenced the bombing of the USS Cole in 2000 and added that compensation should also “be paid to the families of the hundreds of thousands of innocent protestors that Iran has killed over the last 50 years.”

“I have instructed my representatives to put this firmly into any, and all, future negotiations,” he said.

AFP

World.title: 2027: Ortom backs Tinubu, says South should retain presidency
World.content:
stands with Wike, dismisses Atiku link

By Peter Duru, Makurdi

The immediate past Governor of Benue State, Chief Samuel Ortom, has dismissed reports linking him with an alleged arrangement to support former Vice President Atiku Abubakar for the 2027 presidential election, describing the claim as false and baseless.

Ortom, through his Media Assistant, Paul Zege, said his position on the rotation of the presidency to the southern part of Nigeria remained unchanged, insisting that he would not support a return of the presidency to the North in 2027.

Zege, in a statement said the report attributed to a group known as the International Centre for Transparency Nigeria (ICTN) was inconsistent with Ortom’s “well-known and long-standing position on equity, fairness and justice in the leadership of Nigeria.”

According to him, Ortom and four other governors of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), who constituted the G-5 during the build-up to the 2023 elections, had taken a principled position that power should shift to the South after eight years of former President Muhammadu Buhari’s administration.

He said the G-5 position was not motivated by personal animosity against any politician but by the need to promote equity, inclusion, stability and national cohesion in the country.

“Chief Ortom stood firmly by that conviction in 2023 despite the enormous political pressure and consequences that came with it. His position has not changed in 2026 and will not suddenly change because some faceless group has manufactured a political story,” the statement said

The former governor, according to his aide, still believes that the principle which informed the G-5 position in 2023 remains valid ahead of the 2027 presidential election. “Having supported the rotation of the presidency to the South after eight years of a northern presidency, it would amount to a complete contradiction for him to turn around four years later and support the return of the presidency to the North,” he said

The statement therefore declared unequivocally that Ortom believed the presidency should remain in the South in 2027, adding that he had “no reason whatsoever to support Alhaji Atiku Abubakar or any other northern candidate for President in 2027.”

It recalled that Ortom had publicly declared support for President Bola Tinubu’s 2027 re-election during an engagement in Port Harcourt in 2024, saying he had not changed his position.



“His conviction is that the President is the right man for the job, as he has started well and should be supported to complete his major reforms in the country’s economy and overall development,” the statement added.

Ortom also reaffirmed his political alignment with the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, with whom he and other G-5 governors worked together in 2023 in pursuit of what they described as equity and justice.

The former governor said there had been no development to suggest that he had abandoned his position or entered into any political arrangement with Atiku, describing such speculation as a narrative that “collapses under the weight of its own contradictions.”

On meetings between Ortom and other prominent Benue politicians, Zege explained that such engagements were consultations aimed at building a broad strategic alliance of Benue stakeholders for the interest of the state.

He also said Ortom recognised Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Senator George Akume, as the leader of politics in Benue State, stressing that his leadership transcended political party lines.

“Chief Ortom and other like-minded prominent figures in the state are therefore committed to supporting him to succeed in his national assignment,” the statement said, noting that Akume was the first Benue indigene to occupy the influential position of SGF.

The former governor also reaffirmed his support for the PDP governorship candidate in Benue state, Chief Michael Aondoakaa, SAN, describing him as the duly nominated candidate of the party for the 2027 election.

According to Ortom, Aondoakaa possesses the “experience, competence, character and capacity” required to provide purposeful leadership for Benue, adding that he could prudently deploy the state’s increased revenues to tackle development challenges and stimulate economic growth.

Ortom consequently urged the public to disregard the alleged ICTN report, describing it as an attempt by “desperate political elements” to manufacture divisions and create political relationships where none exist.

He maintained that his commitment to equity, justice and fairness remained unwavering, insisting that “no amount of political fabrication will rewrite” the historic position taken by the G-5 governors.

World.title: Customs FOU ‘A’ dismantles ₦3.24bn smuggling syndicate
World.content:
By Godwin Oritse

Operatives of the Federal Operations Unit (FOU), Zone ‘A’, of the Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) have intercepted 220 consignments of prohibited and smuggled goods with a total Duty Paid Value (DPV) of N3.237 billion, while recovering N728.9 million in revenue.



According to the statement signed by Hussaini Abdullahi, Chief Superintendent of Customs and Public Relations officer of the Unit, the operation was driven by enhanced risk profiling, rigorous compliance checks and targeted interventions against suspicious declarations, underscoring the Unit’s sustained commitment to protecting local industries, safeguarding government revenue and keeping Nigeria’s trade corridors free of contraband.



The seizures recorded during the period include 4,956 bags of foreign parboiled rice weighing 50kg each, equivalent to eight trailer loads; 12 foreign-used vehicles; 2,683 parcels of synthetic cannabis (Sativa) weighing 1,439.9kg; 49 parcels of Ghanaian Loud weighing 26.1kg; one parcel of crystal methamphetamine weighing 0.35kg; 13 parcels of granular cannabis weighing 1.35kg; 240,000 tablets of Tramadol; 12,000 tablets of Hypnox; 22 pieces of elephant tusks weighing 130.84kg; 964 25-litre jerry cans of Premium Motor Spirit (PMS), equivalent to 24,100 litres; 26 cartons of foreign vegetable oil containing four 5-litre units each; 686 cartons of foreign poultry products; 414 bales of used clothing; and 2,947 pieces of used tyres, among other prohibited and smuggled items intercepted through intelligence-led operations.



The Comptroller of the Unit, Gambo Aliyu, described the revenue recovery as encouraging and reaffirmed the Unit’s determination to identify and recover revenue lost through under-declaration, false declarations, and other forms of customs fraud.

Aliyu importers, exporters, and licensed customs agents to ensure accurate declarations and full compliance with extant customs laws and regulations, stressing that the Unit would continue to facilitate legitimate trade while taking decisive action against individuals and businesses engaged in smuggling and revenue evasion.

Furthermore, The Unit asserted that the interception of foreign parboiled rice, vegetable oil, poultry products, foreign-used vehicles, used clothing, and other prohibited goods would contribute to protecting domestic industries, supporting national food security, and safeguarding legitimate government revenue. Similarly, the interception of illicit drugs, unregulated pharmaceutical products, and other controlled substances contributes to protecting public health and preventing the circulation of substances capable of undermining the wellbeing of citizens, particularly young Nigerians.



The recovery of elephant tusks also reinforces the Service’s role in supporting national efforts to combat illegal wildlife trafficking and protect endangered species.

The Unit boss emphasised that the Unit’s enforcement activities are being undertaken within a balanced framework that combines robust border enforcement with trade facilitation. He attributed the successes recorded during the period to enhanced intelligence gathering, risk profiling, inter-agency collaboration, intelligence fusion, and the cooperation of stakeholders and members of the public.



He assured compliant traders of the Service’s continued commitment to creating a fair, predictable, and transparent trading environment, while warning that the Unit would sustain its zero-tolerance approach to smuggling, revenue fraud, and other forms of economic sabotage.



The Unit appreciates the continued support of sister agencies, stakeholders, border communities, and members of the public whose intelligence and cooperation contribute significantly to its enforcement efforts.

Comptroller Aliyu called for sustained partnership from the business community and the general public, noting that collective compliance and vigilance remain essential to consolidating the gains recorded in revenue recovery, border protection, public safety, and national economic development.

World.title: I’ll ensure every policeman respects citizens — Edo CP
World.content:
…pledges open-door policing to tackle crime

By Ozioruva Aliu

BENIN CITY — The new Commissioner of Police in Edo State, CP Patrick Daor, has pledged to adopt an open-door policing strategy to combat crime and strengthen public confidence in the state.

Daor also assured residents that every Edo citizen would be treated with respect by personnel of the state police command under his leadership.

The new CP stated this on Monday while assuming office from his predecessor, Monday Agbonika, who has been promoted to Assistant Inspector-General of Police, AIG, Zone 5.

Daor said his administration would intensify the command’s crime-fighting strategies by fine-tuning existing measures and building on the successes recorded by Agbonika.

He said: “More importantly, I will ensure that every policeman has respect for every citizen of this state. We will work towards winning more of the trust of the good people of this state. And we will maintain a very open-door policy.

“Everyone is welcome to contribute. I’m sure you are aware of the popular saying that policing is not just for the police alone. It’s for every one of us.

“Wherever there are issues that you think I should be informed of, please don’t hesitate. Let me know. And that issue will be handled with the utmost professionalism.”

The commissioner also said the command would operate as a highly mobile force capable of responding promptly to security challenges across the state.

“A command that is always moving, addressing every issue that has to do with the good people of the state,” he said.

Earlier, during the official handover ceremony, Agbonika said the command recorded a reduction in crime during his tenure.

He thanked officers and personnel of the command, religious leaders and the Edo State Government for their support during his tenure as commissioner.

World.title: Aiyedatiwa assures persons with albinism of equal opportunities
World.content:
— Distributes sunscreen, sunblocks, cash grants

By Dayo Johnson, Akure

AKURE — Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa of Ondo State has assured persons living with albinism in the state of equal opportunities, saying his administration will not discriminate against them and will ensure their inclusion in government programmes.

The Commissioner for Women Affairs and Social Development, Dr Seun Osamaye, who represented the governor, gave the assurance during the 2026 International Albinism Awareness Day celebration in Akure.

The event was organised by the ministry in collaboration with the Ondo State Agency for the Welfare of Persons with Disabilities.

As part of the programme, 360 tubes of sunscreen, 360 sunblocks and cash assistance were distributed to persons living with albinism to help protect them from skin-related complications.

Osamaye said the administration had taken deliberate steps to end discrimination against persons with disabilities and ensure their participation in government programmes.

“We ensure that we communicate with their leadership and they are given the necessary slots.

“We have decided to choose today as a day to bring together persons with disabilities to create awareness, identify the challenges they face and find solutions that government, stakeholders, individuals and even parents can adopt to ensure that every form of discrimination against them is stopped,” she said.

The theme of this year’s celebration is: “Proudly My Skin: Celebrating All Skin Tones.”

Osamaye described albinism as an inherited genetic condition and not an infectious disease or a curse, urging members of the public to treat persons living with the condition with love, respect and dignity.

“Persons with albinism are known for their unique skin colours. They are easily recognisable.

“But what they have is not by choice. It is hereditary; it is medical. Some of them were born like that. So we should not discriminate against them,” she said.

The commissioner noted that persons with albinism were often underrated and wrongly perceived as incapable, particularly in education and the workplace.

She stressed that they were valuable members of society who deserved equal opportunities, respect and support, while emphasising the importance of early detection in preventing skin cancer.

Osamaye also encouraged persons living with albinism to remain confident and resilient despite societal challenges.

“Don’t look down on yourself, speak up for yourself, put in more effort, and you can achieve whatever you set for yourself,” she said.

The Chairman of the Association of Persons with Albinism in Ondo State, Ayodele Fagorola, commended the governor for his efforts to remove barriers confronting persons living with albinism.

He, however, lamented the continued discrimination and social exclusion faced by the group.

Fagorola identified “acceptability and integration” as major challenges facing persons with albinism in Nigeria and called on state governments to implement deliberate and sustained inclusive policies and programmes.

“Continued stigma and discrimination undermine the sociopolitical and economic contributions persons with albinism make to their communities and the country,” he said.

The Chairman of the State Agency for the Welfare of Persons with Disabilities, Mrs Folashade Arise, commended the state government for its commitment to building an inclusive society.

Arise also praised Governor Aiyedatiwa and the First Lady, Mrs Oluwaseun Aiyedatiwa, for their continued support for persons with disabilities, describing the First Lady as a strong advocate for inclusion.

She also commended officials of the Ministry of Women Affairs and Social Development and the State Agency for the Welfare of Persons with Disabilities for their contributions to the success of the programme.

World.title: Plateau: One-Term Pledge Can’t Replace Devt Plan, PGID Tells Kefiano
World.content:
The Plateau Initiative for Growth and Development has urged the Peoples Democratic Party governorship candidate, Chief Kefas Ropshik Kefiano, to present a detailed development agenda instead of centring his campaign on a pledge to serve only one term.

PIGD made the call in a Monday statement by its National Coordinator, Nengak David, who said the pledge raised questions about the candidate’s priorities and campaign commitments built around zoning.

According to the group, Plateau voters deserve explanations of how Kefiano intends to address insecurity, unemployment, infrastructure, agriculture, education and healthcare.

“The people need to hear what Chief Kefiano will do with power, not merely how long he says he will hold it,” David said. “A one-term pledge cannot substitute for a practical programme showing how the state will be governed and developed.”

PIGD urged Kefiano to explain policies, timelines and measurable targets, allowing voters to assess him on competence and character rather than zonal sentiment.

The organisation also questioned why the electorate should accept the pledge without scrutiny, drawing a comparison with Kefiano’s career in business.

“Chief Kefiano is a businessman who has never publicly declared that he intends to stop making money,” the statement said. “Why, then, should Plateau citizens simply believe that a politician who wins power will willingly surrender it after one term? Such a promise requires more than words; it requires convincing guarantees and demonstrable sincerity.”

The group stressed that its intervention was not directed solely at Kefiano or the PDP, but at candidates and parties across Plateau State.

“We call on politicians, irrespective of party affiliation, to speak honestly to the people,” David said. “Campaigns must be driven by truth, realistic promises and a genuine commitment to service. Plateau has suffered enough from convenient declarations that disappear once elections are over.”

PIGD advised residents to interrogate campaign pledges and demand issue-based engagements from candidates ahead of the election.

“Democracy becomes stronger when citizens refuse to be carried away by sentiment,” it added. “Every candidate must tell Plateau people what will be done, how it will be done and how the public can hold the government accountable.”

World.title: Revenue Monitoring Group Lauds Customs For Bold Reforms in Trade, Security, Technology
World.content:
The Revenue Monitoring Group of Nigeria (RMGN) has commended the Nigeria Customs Service, (NCS) for what it described as “a strategic transformation” in trade facilitation, border security and technology adoption under the leadership of Comptroller-General, Bashir Adewale Adeniyi.

In a statement issued in Abuja on Monday, the civil society organization said the reforms have repositioned Customs beyond revenue collection to become a key driver of national development.

Signed by RMGN President, Dr. Ifeanyi Duruaku, and Secretary General, Comrade Tor Lumun, the group noted that NCS had successfully ditched age-long manual processes in favour of digital, intelligence-led operations.

“The CGC has redefined NCS processes through automation, transparency, and trust with compliant traders,” RMGN stated. “This has fired up operational capacity and unleashed efficiency across the Service.”

The group specifically highlighted the deployment of the Unified Customs Management System, UCMS, and the B’Odogwu platform, which it said have cut human interference, reduced leakages, and sped up cargo clearance.

RMGN also lauded NCS for strengthening collaboration with the Army, Navy, DSS, EFCC and NFIU to combat smuggling, illicit financial flows, and wildlife trafficking.

On global recognition, the group congratulated Dr. Adeniyi on receiving commendation from President Bola Ahmed Tinubu during the 147th/148th sessions of the World Customs Organisation, WCO Council in Brussels on July 3, 2026, where he was unanimously re-elected as Chairperson.

Quoting the President, RMGN stated:

“Adeniyi’s unanimous re-election is not only a personal honour, but also a recognition of Nigeria’s growing influence in global Customs administration. His leadership has been marked by bold initiatives that have improved revenue generation, strengthened border security, facilitated legitimate trade, and modernised Customs operations through homegrown innovations.

“RMGN described the presidential endorsement as “a glowing testament” to the CGC’s achievements.

Reviewing the last three years, the group said the reforms have delivered visible dividends. It cited 2025 trade figures of ₦194.94 trillion, with exports growing by 219.5% to ₦136.65 trillion, attributing the growth to reform and efficiency, not duty hikes.

“In what amounts to a referendum on the current leadership, it is clear that under Dr. Bashir Adewale Adeniyi, the Nigeria Customs Service has been significantly transformed,” RMGN concluded. “We now have a Service that is delivering on revenue, smarter trade facilitation, more effective anti-smuggling operations, and result-driven environmental protection.”

World.title: EU Denies Rejecting INEC Invitation, Confirms Electoral Expert Mission for 2027 Polls
World.content:
Michael Olugbode in Abuja

The European Union (EU) Delegation to Nigeria and ECOWAS has dismissed reports that it rejected an invitation from the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to observe Nigeria’s 2027 general election, describing the reports as inaccurate and speculative.

The EU, in a statement issued in Abuja on Monday, said it had received a formal invitation from INEC dated April 17, 2026, to deploy observers for the 2027 elections.

Contrary to reports that the EU had declined the invitation citing worsening insecurity and alleged hostile treatment of its observers and officials following the publication of its final report on the 2023 general election, the delegation said it had accepted the invitation and would deploy an Electoral Expert Mission (EEM).

It said the response to INEC, dated July 28, 2026, thanked the electoral commission for the invitation and informed it that the EU would field an EEM comprising between two and four independent experts, who would be formally accredited as observers by INEC.

The delegation stressed that the two reasons attributed to the EU in the reports did not appear in its letter to INEC.

“The two alleged reasons mentioned in the press reports do not appear in the letter: these are pure speculations,” the EU said.

According to the delegation, an EEM, like an Electoral Observation Mission, assesses whether an electoral process is conducted in line with international, regional and national obligations and commitments on democratic elections to which the country has subscribed.

The mission will also submit a final report containing recommendations on improving Nigeria’s electoral framework and future electoral processes.

The EU said the report would be shared with the Nigerian government and could subsequently be made available to the wider public if the government agreed.

Explaining its decision to deploy an expert mission rather than a larger electoral observation mission, the delegation said the EU makes decisions annually on electoral missions to partner countries that invite it, with the type of mission determined by the circumstances of each country and the resources available.

“It is on this basis that the decision to conduct an EEM in Nigeria has been taken and will be further consulted with the relevant Nigerian authorities for its implementation,” it stated.

The clarification comes amid growing preparations for the 2027 general election and heightened public interest in the role international partners will play in monitoring Nigeria’s electoral process.

The EU also rejected any suggestion that its decision to deploy an EEM represented a withdrawal of support for democratic governance or Nigeria’s electoral process.

It said the decision “does not affect in any way” the continued implementation of its EU-funded Support to Democratic Governance in Nigeria project, including its support for the electoral process.

The delegation further urged members of the media to verify reports concerning the EU’s positions and statements directly with its press and communication office before publication.

“The EU Delegation respectfully reminds members of the esteemed media community that, to avoid issuing such misleading information about positions or statements of the EU, they can simply check their accuracy with the press and communication office of the EU Delegation,” it said.

The statement, which was signed by the EU Ambassador to Nigeria and ECOWAS, Gautier Mignot, effectively puts to rest reports that the EU had turned down INEC’s invitation to participate in the 2027 electoral process, while confirming that the bloc intends to maintain an independent expert presence during the elections.

World.title: Mastercard Announces New Lead for Eastern Europe, Middle East, Africa region
World.content:
Mastercard has announced that Yasemin Bedir has been appointed President of the company’s Eastern Europe, Middle East and Africa (EEMEA) region, effective 1 September. The company’s EEMEA region was expanded in recent years, bringing additional markets to what is now a vibrant, agile and high growth potential 81 country business.

Bedir, a nearly 20-year veteran of Mastercard, also joins the company’s Management Committee. She succeeds Dimitrios Dosis, who was recently named Chief Commercial Payments Officer, leading Commercial & New Payment Flows.

In this UAE-based role, Bedir will oversee the strategy, direction and overall success of all aspects of Mastercard’s operations across the region through its partnerships with retailers, fintechs, financial institutions, governments and businesses.

“Yasemin is a leader who finds the best in her teams to help them deliver the greatest impact for our customers and to fuel local economies,” said Sachin Mehra, Chief Business Officer, Mastercard. “This is a vast and complex region that demands creative thinking, proven results and strong relationships. Yasemin has delivered that throughout her career. Working with our customers and partners across the EEMEA region, we have a true opportunity to shape and redefine how people and businesses move money, exchange value and enable commerce for years to come.”

Most recently, Bedir served as Division President for Eastern Europe for four years, guiding the team through a complex geopolitical and regulatory environment to strengthen Mastercard’s leadership position across these markets. She is a passionate advocate for talent development and has fostered a culture grounded in accountability and collaboration.

Bedir joined Mastercard in 2007. During her tenure, she gained experience and insights from working in markets across the globe, including serving as General Manager of the company’s Turkey and Azerbaijan activities before overseeing community institution and processor relationships in North America for nearly five years.

“I’ve been inspired by the teams here at Mastercard,” said Bedir. “Their resilience, innovative spirit and relentless dedication to meet and exceed customer needs is what powers our impact every day. Together, we will build on the strong foundation the regional team has created under Dimi’s leadership over the past five years.”

Earlier in her career, Bedir worked at HSBC, Garanti Bank and Yapı Kredi in Turkey. She is among the Founders of the Professional Women Network (PWN) and leads many projects to help SMEs grow.

World.title: Troops Foil ISWAP Attack on FOB Gajiram, Eliminate Extremist Fighters
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

Troops of the Joint Task Force North-East, Operation Hadin Kai (OPHK), have foiled an attack by Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) terrorists on a Forward Operating Base (FOB) in Gajiram, Nganzai Local Government Area of Borno State, the military said.

According to a statement by the Acting Military Information Officer of the Joint Task Force North-East, Operation Hadin Kai, Captain Mohammed Goni, a large number of terrorists launched an assault in an attempt to overrun the troops’ position at about 12:20 a.m. on 10 August 2026.

This is not the first time Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) extremists have attempted to overrun military facilities across the North-East theatre of operations.

Meanwhile, troops have continued to frustrate such attempts, inflicting heavy casualties and recovering weapons from the insurgents.

The Nigerian military has been battling the insurgency for more than a decade and a half.

The statement noted that the gallant troops responded with determined and effective fire, forcing the attackers to withdraw after sustaining heavy casualties.

During the engagement, troops neutralised several terrorists and recovered weapons, ammunition and communication gadgets.

“Post-engagement review of the surveillance footage further confirmed several casualties being evacuated by the retreating terrorists. The recovered items and footage are currently undergoing further operational assessment,” Captain Goni said.

He, however, regretted that a few troops sustained injuries during the engagement after part of the defences was temporarily breached, leading to damage to some combat-enabling equipment and vehicles from rocket-propelled grenade fire.

The injured personnel were promptly airlifted and are currently stable and receiving medical attention.

Captain Goni said: “Following the attack, troops have remained firmly deployed in and around the FOB and adjoining areas to dominate the general area, monitor the situation and prevent any further attempts by the terrorists to re-engage.

“Residents of Gajiram and surrounding communities are advised to remain calm and go about their lawful activities. Members of the public are also encouraged to promptly report any suspicious movement or activity to the nearest security agencies to support intelligence sharing in the ongoing operations.”

Captain Goni said troops would continue to maintain a high level of vigilance in and around Gajiram, while the exploitation of the operational area and further assessment of the terrorists’ casualties and activities remained ongoing.

“Headquarters Theatre Command, Operation Hadin Kai, reassures the public of its unshakable commitment to sustaining pressure on the ISWAP terrorists until lasting peace and stability are fully restored in the North-East,” he concluded.

World.title: Tinubu Welcomes AFCFTA’s Recognition of Nigeria Customs Modernisation Model
World.content:
.Hails Nigerian firm, Bergmans, for winning multi-billion dollar continental customs project

Deji Elumoye in Abuja

President Bola Tinubu has lauded the growing continental recognition of Nigeria’s customs modernisation programme and commended the selection of a subsidiary of Nigerian-owned Bergmans Security Consultant and Supplies Limited for a 20-year, multi-billion-dollar AfCFTA Customs Modernisation Project.

Presidential spokesman, Bayo Onanuga, in a release issued on Monday, disclosed that the project, to be implemented through Bergmans’ subsidiary, AfriTrade CMP Limited, will deploy digital and physical infrastructure to improve customs processes, cargo tracking, border management and trade-data exchange across participating African countries.

Another Bergmans subsidiary, Trade Modernisation Project Limited, is implementing Nigeria’s homegrown customs modernisation programme.

The president said the development validates Nigeria’s capacity to build homegrown solutions for the wider African market.

According to Tinubu, “What has been built and tested in Nigeria is now providing a model for the continent. This is how African integration should work: Africans building African solutions for African opportunities. Nigeria must not only participate in Africa’s single market. Nigerian institutions and businesses can help build the technology and infrastructure that will make that market work. Under our Nigeria First policy, we will continue to create opportunities for capable Nigerian businesses to compete at home, across Africa and globally.

“I commend Bergmans, AfriTrade CMP Limited, Trade Modernisation Project Limited, the Nigeria Customs Service, CGC Bashir Adewale Adeniyi and the Nigerian professionals whose work has earned this confidence.

“The promise of AfCFTA will be realised when goods can move across African borders faster, at lower cost and with fewer barriers. Nigeria is ready to contribute its experience, innovation and enterprise to that future.”

Before now, AfCFTA Secretary-General, Wamkele Mene, had while in Abuja for the agreement, also visited the Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) headquarters to see the Nigerian programme in operation.

Members of the Senate Committee on Customs, led by Senator Jibrin Isah, joined the visit at the conclusion of their two-day retreat on Customs modernisation and reforms.

Mene described B’Odogwu, Nigeria’s indigenous Unified Customs Management System, as a model for Africa and disclosed that non-African companies had offered similar services.

But AfCFTA chose an African solution, underscoring the importance of African excellence and innovation.

Senator Isah, after seeing the systems at work, said members of his committee had become its ambassadors.

B’Odogwu, first piloted in October 2024, has become central to NCS modernisation in Nigeria alongside cargo tracking, data infrastructure, surveillance, risk management and non-intrusive inspection.

The programme is also being integrated with the National Single Window, launched in March 2026 to provide a single digital gateway for cross-border trade processes.

World.title: Police Eliminate Bandit Kingpin Elumah, Recover Weapons in Imo
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Police Special Tactical Squad–Force Intelligence Department (STS-FID) has eliminated a wanted and notorious bandit kingpin, Ojiogu Elumah Martin, also known as “Acid”, in Ohaji/Egbema Local Government Area of Imo State during an intelligence-led raid on his hideout.

According to a statement by the Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Anietie Iniedu, the operation was carried out on 6 August 2026 by STS-FID operatives led by Assistant Commissioner of Police, ACP Victor Ogbeide Godfrey, following the directive of the Inspector-General of Police, IGP Olatunji Disu.

The Force spokesperson revealed that the operation was part of efforts to apprehend those behind the killing of HRH Eze Barrister Paulinus Ekwueme, Ochia I of Ochia Kingdom, his security guards and other persons.

He said: “At about 1:30 a.m. on 6 August 2026, the operatives stormed the hideout of Ojiogu Elumah Martin, alias ‘Acid’, in Ohaji/Egbema. When the suspect saw the police operatives, he opened fire. A gun battle followed and lasted for several hours. The operatives eventually neutralised the suspect.

“The police recovered one AK-47 rifle, three magazines and 56 rounds of 7.62mm live ammunition from the scene. Other members of the gang escaped into the forest during the operation.”

CSP Iniedu said preliminary investigations showed that “Acid” was allegedly the leader of a criminal group linked to several killings and other violent crimes in Ohaji/Egbema and neighbouring communities between 2024 and 2026.

He stressed that the police were still investigating the activities of the group and the roles played by its members.

“Before the latest operation, STS-FID operatives had arrested four suspects and neutralised two other members of the group. One of the suspects arrested earlier was Chinwendo Mirabe, also known as ‘K2’.

“Following the arrest of K2, the police received information that ‘Acid’ allegedly killed Emeka Ebere Nwaele on 12 May 2026. He was said to have suspected that Nwaele had provided information that helped the police arrest one of his gang members. The police are investigating the case as part of the wider investigation into the group,” the statement said.

The notorious bandit, Ojiogu Elumah Martin, is also said to be linked to numerous other violent crimes and acts of economic sabotage in the state.

The Nigeria Police Force assured the people of Ohaji/Egbema and the general public that the investigation would continue.

“The Force will work to arrest all members of the group who escaped during the operation. Anyone found to have taken part in the crimes will be brought to justice.

“The Nigeria Police Force will continue to carry out intelligence-led operations against criminal groups across the country,” the statement assured.

The Force also called on members of the public to provide useful information that could assist the police in arresting fleeing suspects and preventing further crimes.

World.title: Breaking: NERC Dissolves Kaduna Disco Board Over N456.5bn Market Debt
World.content:
Emmanuel Addeh in Abuja

The Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC) has dissolved the board of Kaduna Electricity Distribution Plc (KAEDC) with effect from August 10, 2026, following what it described as severe financial insolvency and prolonged regulatory and market default.

The commission, in an Interim Order, No. NERC/2026/086, issued pursuant to sections 75 to 79 of the Electricity Act 2023, said KAEDC had accumulated more than N118.6 billion in additional market debt under ASI Engineering Limited as of May 2026, taking its total market obligations to approximately N456.5 billion.

NERC said the Disco remitted only 41.93 per cent of its adjusted market invoices in 2025, while its Aggregate Technical, Commercial and Collection (ATC&C) losses stood at 71.88 per cent.

The commission also noted that KAEDC invested just N2.48 billion against a required capital investment of N24.51 billion, while customer metering coverage remained below 36 per cent.

To maintain operational stability and uninterrupted electricity distribution across KAEDC’s franchise area, NERC constituted an interim board of special directors and appointed an administrator for an initial six-month period.

The newly appointed board will be headed by Dr Abdullahi Garba, as Chairman.

NERC also said Afrexim Bank would coordinate a transparent 12-month competitive process to secure a competent replacement core investor for KAEDC.

World.title: RIP | Danny K’s wife Lisa Koppel dies aged 41
World.content:
South African singer Danny K is mourning the death of his wife, Lisa Koppel, with the family asking for privacy following her passing. Image: ChatGPT

South African singer Danny K is mourning the death of his wife, Lisa Koppel, with the family asking for privacy following her passing.

The news was confirmed on Monday by Danny K’s mother, Pam Koppel.

She indicated that the family would not be issuing a formal public statement and that the circumstances surrounding Lisa’s death would remain private.



RIP | Four school learners died this week – South Africa mourns

Deeply saddened by the passing of Lisa Gundelfinger, wife of Danny K.



Our heartfelt thoughts and condolences go out to Danny, their children, and the entire Gundelfinger and Koppel families during this incredibly difficult time.



May Lisa’s memory be a blessing, and may her… pic.twitter.com/fQp88isDuL — Yusuf Abramjee (@Abramjee) August 10, 2026

A life beyond the spotlight

Lisa, the daughter of prominent divorce attorney Billy Gundelfinger, began her career as a model before moving into the legal profession.



She was admitted as an advocate of the High Court in 2010 and went on to build a career in law.

Lisa and Danny K married in 2012 and shared three children.

While Danny K has enjoyed a long and successful career in the South African music industry, Lisa largely maintained a lower public profile, balancing her professional career with family life.



Family tragedy

Lisa’s death is another devastating loss for the Koppel family.

Danny K has previously spoken about the profound impact of losing his brother, Jarren, who died in a helicopter crash in 2003.

Danny K, a multiple South African Music Award winner, has remained one of South Africa’s best-known entertainers since rising to prominence in the early 2000s.



Poem

His father, Gavin Koppel, also appeared to reflect on grief in a poem titled My Promise, which he on Sunday, 9 August.

In the emotional poem, he wrote about turning pain into compassion and vowed: “I will use my pain to heal from this day forward.”

Although Gavin did not explicitly refer to Lisa or confirm her death, the post appeared as news of the family’s loss emerged.



Tributes and messages of condolence have since begun circulating as friends, colleagues and members of the public remember Lisa.

The family has asked for privacy as they mourn her death and support her three children through the difficult period.

World.title: Where pensioners can get private healthcare for free
World.content:
Getting healthcare is either an expensive process or a whole-day event.

Pensioners have a choice between sitting in long queues at a government clinic or paying R650 for a checkup at a local doctor.

That isn’t the case at one private healthcare provider, where pensioners can book an appointment for free.



Free Private Health Care

Clicks launched its Helping Hand Trust in 2011 in partnership with the Western Cape Department of Health (WCDH).

At the time, the initiative was intended to offer baby education, healthcare advice, and basic clinic services to young mothers.

Since then, it has spread nationwide. The service has also expanded.



Now, select Clicks pharmacies offer free basic clinic services on Wednesdays.

To qualify for the free service, pensioners must not have medical aid.

If they do, they will be charged through their medical aid.



Typically, the cost for this service ranges from R120 to R350 depending on the reason for the visit.

On Wednesdays, pensioners can visit a Clicks with a clinic and get a basic checkup for heart health or diabetes.

During these health screenings, the Clicks nurse will check cholesterol levels, measure blood pressure, conduct a glucose test, and offer healthcare advice.



Other free services offered by the retailer include HIV testing and counselling.

Select Clicks’ clinics also offer pap smears, breast exams, and non-invasive prostate screening, but these come at an additional cost.

Booking a Free Clinic Appointment

If your local Clicks has a clinic, you can wait in the queue from 08:00 to 17:00 on Wednesdays.



However, to skip the queue, you can book an appointment online by visiting the Clicks website.

When booking an appointment, you need to select the services with “Helping Hand” in the title.

It’s possible to make an appointment for up to four people. Confirmation will be sent via sms and email.



Pensioners can also book their Helping Hand appointment by dialling the retailer’s customer service line.

Affordable Private Healthcare for Pensioners

Pensioners who want affordable private healthcare through their medical aid can also use Clicks.

The retailer offers premium clinic services between Monday and Friday.



In addition to the heart health and diabetes screening, Clicks offers:

Flu vaccinations

Pneumonia vaccination

Vitamin injections

They also have a nurse-assisted virtual doctor consultation.

During these sessions, the doctor guides the consultation, and the nurse will assist.



Dischem offers similar services.

Dischem nurses provide basic clinic services, but they can also lead a virtual doctor appointment.

These consultations are roughly 45% cheaper than an in-person consultation at a local doctor.

World.title: Two weeks later: Search continues for missing Cape Town siblings
World.content:
Two weeks after they went missing, police say the search for Elsies River siblings Perez, Atarah and Alessia Khumalo continues. Image: The Pink Ladies

Two weeks on, three Elsies River children remain missing as police press on with the search to bring them home.

Alessia Khumalo, 7, Perez Khumalo, 4, and one-year-old Atarah Khumalo were last seen at their Bestenbier Avenue home on 27 July. It’s alleged they left with their dad to get ice-cream at around 12:00 on the day.

Western Cape police have confirmed that the search remains active.



No breakthrough yet

Police spokesperson Captain FC van Wyk said detectives are still working to trace the children.

“The matter you are referring to is still under investigation. The search and investigations continue,” Van Wyk said.

No arrests have been announced.

Police previously confirmed that the siblings were last seen with a man identified as their father. He has not been publicly named as a suspect.



What the siblings were wearing

When they were last seen, Alessia was wearing a blue-and-yellow tracksuit with black shoes. Atarah was dressed in a pink tracksuit and pink shoes, while Perez was wearing a grey tracksuit with black tekkies.

Community appeal continues

The disappearance has left the Elsies River community searching for answers. Missing-persons organisations and residents have continued to circulate appeals for information.

Earlier this week, missing persons organisation The Pink Ladies also appealed to the public for help to find the children after issuing a missing persons alert.



Police urge anyone who may have seen the children or has information about their whereabouts to come forward.

Information can be shared anonymously through Crime Stop on 08600 10111 or via the MySAPS App.

World.title: Sharks lose Springbok forward on eve of All Blacks game
World.content:
The Sharks will be without Vincent Tshituka against the All Blacks. Image: SA Rugby

The All Blacks have opted to select a powerful side for Tuesday’s second tour game against the Sharks, but unfortunately the home side will be far from its best.

“We’ve got a lot of injuries, and we are midway in pre-season,” Sharks coach JP Pietersen admitted on the eve of the match.

Besides injury concerns to Springboks Bongi Mbonambi, Makazole Mapimpi, Jordan and Jaden Hendrikse, Vincent Tshituka has also been ruled out due to concussion.



“I’ll hold my fingers and toes together for tomorrow, but we prepare the boys as best as we can to give them a good opportunity to be robust and competitive against the All Blacks,” Pietersen added.

“We’ll see tomorrow how it goes and obviously we will not be at 100% – at best at 70 or 80% – but we’ll give it everything we can and we’ll see how it goes.”

World.title: OPEN | West Coast National Park welcomes visitors to wildflower season
World.content:
The highly anticipated 2026 wildflower season is officially underway at West Coast National Park. Don't miss it! Image: SANParks

The highly anticipated 2026 wildflower season is officially underway at West Coast National Park, with visitors able to experience the annual floral spectacle from 1 August to 30 September.

The iconic Postberg section opened to the public on Saturday, 1 August, giving visitors access to one of South Africa’s most spectacular seasonal displays.

SEE | Namaqua National Park in full colour as wildflower season blooms



While some flower species have appeared earlier than usual this year, SANParks says the timing, spread and intensity of the display will continue to depend on weather conditions throughout the season.

Visitors can therefore expect the landscape to change significantly over the coming weeks as more species emerge and reach peak bloom.

Thousands expected to visit

The flower season is one of West Coast National Park’s busiest periods, attracting visitors from across South Africa and internationally.



During August 2025 alone, the park welcomed more than 23 000 visitors, while the Postberg section recorded approximately 7 500 vehicle entries over the course of the flower season.

SANParks is expecting another strong turnout this year as visitors head to the park to see the colourful carpets of indigenous wildflowers.

Best time to see the flowers

Visitors hoping to get the best views are advised to plan their trips according to the weather.



Flower viewing is typically at its best on sunny days between late morning and mid-afternoon, when the flowers are fully open.

The display can vary considerably depending on rainfall, temperature and sunshine, meaning conditions may change from one week to the next.

Wildflower guide available

Visitors can also purchase the popular Spring Flowers Booklet at the Postberg entrance gate.



The guide was developed by the West Coast Region SANParks Honorary Rangers as a fundraising initiative and helps visitors identify the wide variety of wildflowers found throughout the park.

Proceeds also contribute towards conservation initiatives.

SANParks is encouraging visitors to plan ahead during the busy season and to follow its official channels for regular updates on flower conditions.



The Postberg section will remain open until 30 September 2026, weather and park conditions permitting.

World.title: Orange level 6 weather warnings
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - A bitter blast is gripping parts of South Africa, with dangerous weather disrupting lives and travel.

The South African Weather Service has issued an Orange Level 6 warning for disruptive snow, with parts of the Eastern Cape and Free State among the hardest hit.

Eastern Cape authorities said a total of five mountain passes in the high-lying areas of the Eastern Cape remain closed to traffic as snowfall continues to affect parts of the province.

* Barkly Pass – R58 between Ekhephini (Barkly East) and Khowa (Elliot)

* ⁠Penhoek Pass - N6 between Komani and James Calata (Jamestown)

* ⁠Boesmanshoek Pass - between Sterkstroom and Molteno

* ⁠Qashas Nek Pass – between Matatiele and Lesotho

* ⁠Lootsberg Pass – N9 between Robert Sobukwe (Graaff-Reinet) and Middelburg

Alternative route for N9: From Graaff-Reinet, use the N9/N6 towards the R61 to Nxuba, then rejoin the N10 towards Middelburg.

All other mountain passes remain open, but motorists are urged to exercise extreme caution as winter conditions may change rapidly.

"Avoid closed routes, obey road closure signs and follow instructions from traffic and emergency personnel."

Yellow Level 2 snow warnings are also in place, while damaging winds are expected along parts of the KwaZulu-Natal coast.

Gauteng is bracing for severe thunderstorms as the weather turns increasingly treacherous.

World.title: What next for beleaguered FIFA president Infantino?
World.content:
